sentences.zh: 【魏紀八】起昭陽作噩，盡旃蒙大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Wei Records 8] From Zhaoyang Zuoe through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Wei, Number Eight] Spanning from the cyclical year Zhaoyang Zuoe through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian—three years in all.

translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Duke of Shaoling, fifth year of Jiaping (

translations.idiomatic: the year guiyou, AD 253)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，朔，蜀大將軍費禕與諸將大會於漢壽，郭循在坐；

translations.literal: In spring, on the first day of the first month, Shu Grand General Fei Yi held a great assembly with the various generals at Hanshou; Guo Xun was among those seated;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, the Shu Grand General Fei Yi held a grand council with his commanders at Hanshou, with Guo Xun in attendance;

sentences.zh: 禕歡飲沉醉，循起刺禕，殺之。

translations.literal: Yi drank merrily and became deeply intoxicated; Xun rose and stabbed Yi, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi drank freely until he was thoroughly drunk; Xun sprang up and stabbed him to death.

sentences.zh: 禕資性泛愛，不疑於人。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was broadly affectionate; he did not suspect others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Yi was open-hearted and trusting; he did not doubt others.

sentences.zh: 越巂太守張嶷嘗以書戒之日：「昔岑彭率師，來歙杖節，鹹見害於刺客。

translations.literal: Yuexi Commandery Administrator Zhang Ni once admonished him in a letter, saying: "In former times Cen Peng led armies and Lai Xi bore the staff of authority—both alike fell victim to assassins.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni, Administrator of Yuexi, had once warned him in a letter: "In the past Cen Peng led troops in the field and Lai Xi held imperial commission—both were cut down by assassins.

sentences.zh: 今明將軍位尊權重，待信新附太過，宜鑒前事，少以為警。

translations.literal: Now, illustrious general, your position is exalted and your authority weighty; you trust and treat the newly attached too generously. You should take the former cases as a mirror and be somewhat on your guard.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you hold high rank and heavy authority, you place too much trust in men who have only lately submitted. Take those precedents as your warning and keep somewhat on your guard.

sentences.zh: 」禕不從，故及禍。

translations.literal: " Yi did not follow this advice, and therefore met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi did not heed him, and so came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 詔追封郭循為長樂鄉侯，使其子襲爵。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Guo Xun as Marquis of Changle District and had his son inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Guo Xun as Marquis of Changle District and allowed his son to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 王昶、毌丘儉聞東軍敗，各燒屯走。

translations.literal: Wang Chang and Guanqiu Jian, hearing that the eastern army had been defeated, each burned their camps and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chang and Guanqiu Jian heard that the eastern army had been defeated, each burned his camps and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲貶黜諸將，大將軍師曰：「我不聽公休，以至於此。

translations.literal: At court it was proposed to demote and dismiss the various generals. The Grand General Sima Shi said: "I did not heed Gongxiu, and matters came to this.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated demoting the commanders, but Grand General Sima Shi said, "I refused to listen to Gongxiu, and that is how we came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 此我過也，諸將何罪！

translations.literal: This is my fault—what crime have the generals committed!
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine—what crime have the generals committed?

sentences.zh: 」悉宥之。

translations.literal: " He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: " He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 師弟安東將軍昭時為監軍，唯削昭爵而已。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Sima Zhao, then General Who Pacifies the East and army supervisor, had only his noble rank reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Sima Zhao, then General Who Pacifies the East serving as army supervisor, was merely stripped of his noble rank.

sentences.zh: 以諸葛誕為鎮南將軍，都督豫州；

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan was made General Who Guards the South and area commander of Yuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan was appointed General Who Guards the South and put in command of Yuzhou;

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉為鎮東將軍，都督揚州。

translations.literal: Guanqiu Jian was made General Who Guards the East and area commander of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian was appointed General Who Guards the East and put in command of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，雍州刺史陳泰求敕并州並力討胡，師從之。

translations.literal: That year, Inspector of Yongzhou Chen Tai requested an imperial order that Bingzhou join forces to campaign against the barbarians; Shi approved it.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chen Tai, Inspector of Yongzhou, asked that Bingzhou be ordered to join him in campaigning against the barbarians, and Shi agreed.

sentences.zh: 未集，而雁門、新興二郡胡以遠役，遂驚反。

translations.literal: Before the forces had assembled, the barbarians of Yanmen and Xinxing commanderies, alarmed by the distant service, rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies could assemble, the barbarians of Yanmen and Xinxing, alarmed by the prospect of distant service, rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 師又謝朝士曰：「此我過也，非陳雍州之責！

translations.literal: Shi again apologized to the court officials, saying: "This is my fault, not the responsibility of Chen of Yongzhou!
translations.idiomatic: Shi again apologized to the court, saying, "This is my fault, not Chen Tai's responsibility!

sentences.zh: 」是以人皆愧悅。

translations.literal: " Therefore everyone felt both ashamed and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone was moved to shame and admiration.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒論曰：司馬大將軍引二敗以為己過，過消而業隆，可謂智矣。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi commented: The Grand General Sima took two defeats upon himself as his own fault; the fault was dispelled and his enterprise flourished—this may be called wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi remarked: By taking two defeats upon himself, Grand General Sima dispelled blame and strengthened his position—this was true wisdom.

sentences.zh: 若乃諱敗推過，歸咎萬物，常執其功而隱其喪，上下離心，賢愚解體，謬之甚矣！

translations.literal: As for concealing defeat and shifting blame, attributing guilt to all around, always seizing credit while hiding losses—superiors and subordinates lose heart, the worthy and the foolish fall apart: how grievously mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: To conceal defeat, shift blame, claim every success while hiding every loss—when superiors and subordinates lose heart and talent disperses, the error could hardly be greater!

sentences.zh: 君人者，苟統斯理而以御國，行失而名揚，兵挫而戰勝，雖百敗可也，況於再乎！

translations.literal: One who rules men, if he grasps this principle and thereby governs the state, may act wrongly yet win renown, suffer military setbacks yet achieve victory—even a hundred defeats are bearable, how much more two!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who masters this principle may err in conduct yet grow in fame, suffer defeat in battle yet win the war—even a hundred setbacks are tolerable, let alone two!

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫張緝言於師曰：「恪雖克捷，見誅不久。

translations.literal: Minister of the Household Zhang Ji said to Shi: "Although Ke has won victory, he will soon be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Household Zhang Ji told Shi, "Ke may have won his battle, but he will soon be executed.

sentences.zh: 」師曰：「何故？

translations.literal: " Shi said: "For what reason?
translations.idiomatic: " Shi asked, "Why do you say so?

sentences.zh: 」緝曰：「威震其主，功蓋一國，求不得死乎！

translations.literal: " Ji said: "His authority overawes his lord, his achievements overshadow the whole state—can he hope to escape death!
translations.idiomatic: " Ji replied, "His might overawes his sovereign and his achievements overshadow the realm—how could he hope to die a natural death?

sentences.zh: 二月，吳軍還自東興。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Wu army returned from Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Wu army returned from Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 進封太傅恪陽都侯，加荊、揚州牧，督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Ke was advanced in rank to Marquis of Yangdu, made Governor of Jing and Yang provinces, and put in overall command of all military affairs at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke was promoted to Marquis of Yangdu, made Governor of Jing and Yang, and given supreme command over all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 恪遂有輕敵之心，復欲出軍。

translations.literal: Ke thereupon grew contemptuous of the enemy and wished again to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: Ke grew overconfident and wished to march out again.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣以為數出罷勞，同辭諫恪，恪不聽。

translations.literal: The various ministers held that repeated campaigns had exhausted the troops and, with one voice, remonstrated with Ke; Ke would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers argued that repeated campaigns had worn the army down and jointly urged Ke to desist; he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 中散大夫蔣延固爭，恪命扶出。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Jiang Yan argued stubbornly; Ke ordered him carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Jiang Yan pressed his objections relentlessly until Ke had him bodily removed.

sentences.zh: 因著論以諭眾曰：「凡敵國欲相吞，即仇讎欲相除也。

translations.literal: He thereupon composed a treatise to instruct the multitude, saying: "Whenever enemy states wish to swallow one another, it is like sworn foes wishing to destroy each other.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a treatise to instruct his colleagues: "When rival states seek to devour one another, it is like sworn enemies striving to destroy each other.

sentences.zh: 有仇而長之，禍不在己，則在後人，不可不為遠慮也。

translations.literal: If one has an enemy and allows him to grow strong, the calamity will fall not on oneself but on later generations—one cannot fail to plan far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: If you let an enemy grow strong, the disaster may not strike you but your descendants—long-term planning is indispensable.

sentences.zh: 昔秦但得關西耳，尚以併吞六國。

translations.literal: In former times Qin held only the lands west of the passes, yet still went on to annex the Six States.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Qin held only the lands west of the passes, yet still went on to swallow the Six States.

sentences.zh: 今以魏比古之秦，土地數倍；

translations.literal: Now, comparing Wei to Qin of old, its territory is several times as large;
translations.idiomatic: Today Wei compared with ancient Qin commands several times the territory;

sentences.zh: 以吳與蜀，比古六國，不能半也。

translations.literal: while Wu and Shu together, compared with the Six States of old, amount to less than half.
translations.idiomatic: while Wu and Shu together amount to less than half the Six States.

sentences.zh: 然今所以能敵之者，但以操時兵眾，於今適盡，而後生者未及長大，正是賊衰少未盛之時。

translations.literal: Yet the reason we can contend with them now is simply that the troops Cao Cao raised have by now just been used up, while those born later have not yet grown to maturity—this is precisely when the foe is declining and not yet at its height.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we can still contend with them only because the armies Cao Cao raised are now exhausted and the next generation has not yet come of age—precisely when the enemy is weak and not yet at full strength.

sentences.zh: 加司馬懿先誅王凌，續自隕斃，其子幼弱而專彼大任，雖有智計之士，未得施用。

translations.literal: Moreover Sima Yi first executed Wang Ling and then himself perished in succession; his son is young and weak yet holds that great responsibility alone—even men of strategy and counsel cannot be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Sima Yi first executed Wang Ling and then died in turn; his son is young and weak yet holds supreme power alone—even able strategists cannot put their talents to use.

sentences.zh: 當今伐之，是其厄會。

translations.literal: To attack them now is to strike at their hour of crisis.
translations.idiomatic: To attack them now is to strike at their moment of crisis.

sentences.zh: 聖人急於趨時，誠謂今日。

translations.literal: The sage hurries to seize the moment—truly this is that day.
translations.idiomatic: The sage hurries to seize the hour—and that hour is today.

sentences.zh: 若順眾人之情，懷偷安之計，以為長江之險可以傳世，不論魏之終始而以今日遂輕其後，此吾所以長歎息者也！

translations.literal: If we follow the feelings of the multitude, harbor plans for ease and comfort, think the Yangzi's peril can be passed down through generations, and without weighing Wei's beginning and end lightly regard today and neglect what follows—this is why I sigh long and deep!
translations.idiomatic: If we follow popular sentiment, cling to ease, imagine the Yangzi's defenses can shield us forever, and without weighing Wei's long-term prospects treat today lightly and neglect tomorrow—that is what makes me sigh in despair!

sentences.zh: 今聞眾人或以百姓尚貧，欲務閒息，此不知慮其大危而愛其小勤者也。

translations.literal: Now I hear that some, because the common people are still poor, wish to pursue rest and ease—this is failing to reckon with great peril while cherishing small exertion.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear some say the people are still poor and we should seek repose—this is to ignore grave danger for the sake of sparing a little toil.

sentences.zh: 昔漢祖幸已自有三秦之地，何不閉關守險以自娛樂，空出攻楚，身被創痍，介冑生蟣虱，將士厭困苦，豈甘鋒刃而忘安寧哉？

translations.literal: In former times the Founder of Han, having already possessed the Three Qin, why did he not close the passes and guard the perilous terrain for his own pleasure, but instead marched out in vain to attack Chu—his body covered with wounds, lice breeding in his armor, his officers and men weary of hardship? Did they relish the blade and forget peace?
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder of Han already held the Three Qin, why did he not shut the passes and enjoy his security, but marched out against Chu—his body covered with wounds, lice in his armor, his men worn down by hardship? Did they love the sword and forget peace?

sentences.zh: 慮於長久不得兩存者耳。

translations.literal: He was concerned that in the long run both could not coexist.
translations.idiomatic: He understood that in the long run both sides could not coexist.

sentences.zh: 每覽荊邯說公孫述以進取之圖，近見家叔父表陳與賊爭競之計，未嘗不喟然歎息也！

translations.literal: Whenever I read how Jing Han urged Gongsun Shu with plans for advance, or recently saw my uncle's memorial setting forth schemes to contend with the foe, I have never failed to sigh deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read how Jing Han urged Gongsun Shu toward conquest, or lately saw my uncle's memorial on competing with the enemy, I cannot help but sigh!

sentences.zh: 夙夜反側，所慮如此，故聊疏愚言，以達二、三君子之末。

translations.literal: Day and night I toss restlessly with such concerns in mind; therefore I briefly set down these humble words to reach two or three gentlemen at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I lie awake with these worries; I set down these humble words to reach two or three of you who share my concern.

sentences.zh: 若一朝隕沒，志畫不立，貴令來世知我所憂，可思於後耳。

translations.literal: If I should one morning perish and my plans not be established, it would be precious to let later ages know what I worried over, so they may reflect upon it hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: If I should die tomorrow and my designs go unrealized, let later ages know what I feared, that posterity may take thought from it.

sentences.zh: 」眾人雖皆心以為不可，然莫敢復難。

translations.literal: " Although everyone in his heart thought it unwise, none dared argue again.
translations.idiomatic: " Though all still thought him wrong at heart, none dared object again.

sentences.zh: 丹楊太守聶友素與恪善，以書諫恪曰：「大行皇帝本有遏東關之計，計未施行；

translations.literal: Danyang Administrator Nie You, who had long been on good terms with Ke, admonished him in a letter, saying: "The late emperor originally had a plan to check Dongguan, but the plan was not carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Nie You, Administrator of Danyang and an old friend of Ke's, wrote to dissuade him: "The late emperor had planned to block Dongguan, but the plan was never executed;

sentences.zh: 今公輔贊大業，成先帝之志，寇遠自送，將士憑賴威德，出身用命，一旦有非常之功，豈非宗廟神靈社稷之福邪！

translations.literal: now you assist and uphold the great enterprise, fulfilling the late emperor's will; the foe came from afar of his own accord, and the officers and men, relying on your authority and virtue, gave their lives in service and in a single stroke achieved extraordinary merit—is this not a blessing from the ancestral temples, the spirits, and the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: now you uphold the great enterprise and fulfill the late emperor's will; the enemy came to us from afar, and your men, trusting in your authority, fought with their lives and won a signal victory—is this not a blessing from the ancestral spirits and the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 宜且案兵養銳，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: You should for now hold the armies in check and nurture their edge, watch for openings and then act.
translations.idiomatic: You should hold your armies in check, restore their strength, watch for an opening, and then strike.

sentences.zh: 今乘此勢欲復大出，天時未可而苟任盛意，私心以為不安。

translations.literal: Now, riding this momentum you wish again to take the field on a grand scale—the season is not right, yet you stubbornly follow your ardor; in my private heart I find this unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: Now you wish to march out again on the strength of this victory—the timing is wrong, yet you insist on your zeal; privately I find this troubling.

sentences.zh: 」恪題論後，為書答友曰：「足下雖有自然之理，然未見大數，熟省此論，可以開悟矣。

translations.literal: " After Ke had inscribed his treatise at the end, he wrote in reply to You: "You, sir, have natural reason on your side, yet you have not seen the larger pattern; study this treatise carefully and you may be enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke appended his treatise and wrote back: "You speak with sound reason, yet you have not grasped the larger design; read this treatise carefully and you may see the light.

sentences.zh: 滕胤謂恪曰：「君受伊、霍之托，入安本朝，出摧強敵，名聲振於海內，天下莫不震動，萬姓之心，冀得蒙君而息。

translations.literal: Teng Yin said to Ke: "You received the trust of an Yi Yin or Huo Guang—within you pacified the court, without you crushed a powerful foe; your fame resounds across the seas, all under Heaven is shaken, and the hearts of the myriad people hope to find rest under your protection.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin told Ke, "You were entrusted as Yi Yin and Huo Guang were—within you pacified the court, without you crushed a mighty foe; your fame rings across the realm, all under Heaven trembles, and the people long to rest under your protection.

sentences.zh: 今猥以勞役之後，興師出征，民疲力屈，遠主有備，若攻城不克，野略無獲，是喪前勞而招後責也。

translations.literal: Now, rashly after labor and campaigns, you raise armies and march forth—the people are exhausted in strength, the distant lord is on guard; if you cannot take cities by assault and gain nothing in the countryside, you will squander former toil and invite blame hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Now, right after heavy labor and campaigns, you would march out again—the people are exhausted, the distant enemy is prepared; if sieges fail and raids gain nothing, you will waste past effort and invite future blame.

sentences.zh: 不如案甲息師，觀隙耐勸。

translations.literal: Better to lay aside armor and rest the troops, watch for gaps and await the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: Better to lay aside your armor, rest your troops, watch for openings, and wait for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 且兵者大事，事以眾濟，眾苟不悅，君獨安之！

translations.literal: Moreover war is a great matter; affairs succeed through the multitude—if the multitude is not pleased, how can you alone be at ease!
translations.idiomatic: War is a grave matter—it succeeds only with popular support; if the people are discontent, how can you alone be at ease?

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「諸雲不可，皆不見計算，懷居苟安者也。

translations.literal: " Ke said: "All say it cannot be done—they none see the reckoning and are men who cling to comfort and seek only ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke replied, "Everyone says no—they none see the calculation and are men who cling to comfort and ease.

sentences.zh: 而子復以為然，吾何望乎！

translations.literal: Yet you too think them right—what hope have I left!
translations.idiomatic: And you agree with them—what hope have I left!

sentences.zh: 夫以曹芳暗劣，而政在私門，彼之民臣，固有離心。

translations.literal: As for Cao Fang, he is dim and inferior, while government lies in private hands—their people and ministers naturally harbor divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fang is dim-witted and weak, while power rests in private hands—their people and officials are already divided in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今吾因國家之資，藉戰勝之威，則何往而不克哉！

translations.literal: Now, relying on the state's resources and borrowing the prestige of victory—where could we go and not prevail!
translations.idiomatic: With the state's resources and the prestige of victory behind us—where could we march and not prevail?

sentences.zh: 三月，恪大發州郡二十萬眾復入寇，以滕胤為都下督，掌統留事。

translations.literal: In the third month, Ke mustered two hundred thousand men from the provinces and commanderies and again invaded; he made Teng Yin metropolitan supervisor to oversee affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ke mobilized two hundred thousand men from the provinces and invaded again, leaving Teng Yin as metropolitan supervisor to manage affairs at home.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 漢姜維自以練西方風俗，兼負其才武，欲誘諸羌、胡以為羽翼，謂自隴以西，可斷而有。

translations.literal: Shu's Jiang Wei, considering himself versed in the customs of the western regions and confident in his talent and martial prowess, wished to entice the various Qiang and barbarians as his wings, believing that from Long westward the territory could be severed and possessed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei of Shu, confident that he knew the western frontier and trusting in his talent and martial skill, sought to win over the Qiang and other barbarians as allies, believing he could cut off and hold everything west of Long.

sentences.zh: 每欲興軍大舉，費禕常裁製不從。

translations.literal: Whenever he wished to raise armies on a grand scale, Fei Yi would restrain and curb him and not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wished to launch a major campaign, Fei Yi would restrain him and refuse consent.

sentences.zh: 與其兵不過萬人，曰：「吾等不如丞相亦已遠矣，丞相猶不能定中夏，況吾等乎！

translations.literal: He gave him no more than ten thousand troops, saying: "We fall far short of the Chancellor as it is; the Chancellor still could not settle the Central Plains—how much less can we!
translations.idiomatic: He allowed him no more than ten thousand men, saying, "We are far beneath the Chancellor already, and even he could not pacify the Central Plains—how much less can we!

sentences.zh: 不如且保國治民，謹守社稷，如其功業，以俟能者，無為希冀徼幸，決成敗於一舉；

translations.literal: Better for now to preserve the state and govern the people, guard the altars of state with care, and if achievements are to come, await able men; do not hope for luck or stake success and failure on a single stroke;
translations.idiomatic: Better to preserve the state, govern the people, and guard the altars with care; if great deeds are to come, let abler men attempt them—do not gamble everything on one throw;

sentences.zh: 若不如志，悔之無及。

translations.literal: if your wishes are not fulfilled, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: if you fail, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 」及禕死，維得行其志，乃將數萬人出石營，圍狄道。

translations.literal: " When Yi died, Wei was able to carry out his will; he then led several tens of thousands of men out from Shiying and besieged Didao.
translations.idiomatic: " After Yi's death Wei was free to act on his designs; he led tens of thousands out from Shiying and besieged Didao.

sentences.zh: 吳諸葛恪入寇淮南，驅略民人。

translations.literal: Wu's Zhuge Ke invaded Huainan and drove off and plundered the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke of Wu invaded Huainan, driving off and plundering the populace.

sentences.zh: 諸將或謂恪曰：「今引軍深入，疆場之民，必相率遠遁，恐兵勞而功少，不如止圍新城，新城困，救必至，至而圖之，乃可大獲。

translations.literal: Some of the generals said to Ke: "Now that you lead the army deep in, the people of the borderlands will surely flee far away in groups—we fear the troops will toil while the gains are few. Better to stop and besiege Xincheng; when Xincheng is distressed, relief is sure to come, and when it comes we can plan against it—then we may reap a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Some generals urged Ke, "Marching deep inland, the border people will flee en masse—we risk exhausting our men for little gain. Better to halt and besiege Xincheng; when the city is desperate, relief will come, and we can strike the relief force for a great prize.

sentences.zh: 」恪從其計，五月，還軍圍新城。

translations.literal: " Ke followed this plan; in the fifth month he turned the army back to besiege Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke agreed; in the fifth month he turned back to besiege Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 詔太尉司馬孚督諸軍二十萬往赴之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Commandant Sima Fu to supervise an army of two hundred thousand to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Grand Commandant Sima Fu to take command of two hundred thousand men and march to the relief.

sentences.zh: 大將軍師問於虞松曰：「今東西有事，二方皆急，而諸將意沮，若之何？

translations.literal: Grand General Shi asked Yu Song: "Now there are troubles east and west; both fronts are urgent, yet the generals' spirits are dampened—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Shi asked Yu Song, "We face crises on both fronts, yet the generals are disheartened—what should we do?

sentences.zh: 」松曰：「昔周亞夫堅壁昌邑而吳、楚自敗，事有似弱而強，不可不察也。

translations.literal: " Song said: "In former times Zhou Yafu held fast behind walls at Changyi and Wu and Chu defeated themselves—affairs may seem weak yet prove strong; this cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: " Song replied, "When Zhou Yafu held fast at Changyi, Wu and Chu defeated themselves—what looks weak may prove strong; this must be weighed carefully.

sentences.zh: 今恪悉其銳眾，足以肆暴，而坐守新城，欲以致一戰耳。

translations.literal: Now Ke has concentrated all his elite troops, enough to run riot, yet sits guarding Xincheng—he wishes to provoke a single decisive battle, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Ke has massed his best troops, enough to ravage the countryside, yet sits before Xincheng—he wants to force a decisive battle, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 若攻城不拔，請戰不可，師老眾疲，勢將自走，諸將之不徑進，乃公之利也。

translations.literal: If he cannot take the city by assault and cannot obtain the battle he seeks, his army will age and his troops grow weary, and the momentum will carry him off of itself—the generals' not pressing forward directly is to your advantage.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot storm the city or draw you into battle, his army will wear out and withdraw of its own accord—the generals' reluctance to advance is actually to your advantage.

sentences.zh: 姜維有重兵而縣軍應恪，投食我麥，非深根之寇也。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei has a heavy force but has left his army exposed to support Ke, casting himself upon our grain for food—he is not a foe with deep roots.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei has a large force but has marched out lightly to support Ke, living off our wheat—he is no deeply rooted invader.

sentences.zh: 且謂我並力於東，西方必虛，是以徑進。

translations.literal: Moreover he thinks we are concentrating all strength in the east and that the west must be empty—therefore he advances directly.
translations.idiomatic: He assumes we are committing everything to the east and that the west must be undefended—that is why he pushes straight in.

sentences.zh: 今若使關中諸軍倍道急赴，出其不意，殆將走矣。

translations.literal: Now if we have the armies of Guanzhong march at double speed in urgent haste and take him unawares, he will likely flee.
translations.idiomatic: If the Guanzhong armies march at forced pace and take him by surprise, he will likely flee.

sentences.zh: 」師曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Shi said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」乃使郭淮、陳泰悉關中之眾，解狄道之圍；

translations.literal: " He then sent Guo Huai and Chen Tai with all the forces of Guanzhong to relieve the siege of Didao;
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Guo Huai and Chen Tai with all the Guanzhong forces to lift the siege of Didao;

sentences.zh: 敕毌丘儉等案兵自守，以新城委吳。

translations.literal: he ordered Guanqiu Jian and the others to hold their armies in check and defend on their own, leaving Xincheng to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Guanqiu Jian and the others to hold their positions and leave Xincheng to Wu.

sentences.zh: 陳泰進至洛門，姜維糧盡，退還。

translations.literal: Chen Tai advanced to Luomen; Jiang Wei's provisions were exhausted and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai advanced to Luomen; Jiang Wei ran out of supplies and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 揚州牙門將涿郡張特守新城。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Gate Commander Zhang Te of Zhuo Commandery defended Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Te of Zhuo, gate commander of Yangzhou, held Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 吳人攻之連月，城中兵合三千人，疾病戰死者過半，而恪起土山急攻，城將陷，不可護。

translations.literal: The Wu forces attacked for months on end; the troops in the city totaled three thousand, and more than half had died of illness or in battle; Ke raised earthen mounds for urgent assault, the city was about to fall and could not be defended.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu besieged it for months; the garrison numbered three thousand, more than half dead of sickness or battle; Ke built earthen ramps for a furious assault, and the city was about to fall beyond all defense.

sentences.zh: 特乃謂吳人曰：「今我無心復戰也。

translations.literal: Te then said to the Wu men: "I have no heart to fight further.
translations.idiomatic: Te then told the Wu besiegers, "I have no will to fight on.

sentences.zh: 然魏法，被攻過百日而救不至者，雖降，家不坐；

translations.literal: Yet by Wei law, if one has been under attack for more than a hundred days and relief has not arrived, even if one surrenders the household is not punished;
translations.idiomatic: But by Wei law, if a city has been besieged over a hundred days without relief, even those who surrender are not punished along with their families;

sentences.zh: 自受敵以來，已九十餘日矣，此城中本有四千餘人，戰死者已過半，城雖陷，尚有半人不欲降，我當還為相語，條別善惡，明日早送名，且以我印綬去為信。

translations.literal: since we met the enemy it has already been more than ninety days; this city originally had more than four thousand men, and over half have died in battle; though the city is about to fall, still half the people do not wish to surrender. I should go back and speak with them, sorting out good and bad; tomorrow morning I will send the roster of names, and for now take my seal and ribbon as proof.
translations.idiomatic: we have been under attack for more than ninety days; the city once held over four thousand, more than half now dead; though the walls are failing, half the men still refuse to yield. Let me go back and confer with them, sort the willing from the unwilling, and send you the roster tomorrow; take my seal and ribbon as pledge.

sentences.zh: 」乃投其印綬與之。

translations.literal: " He then cast his seal and ribbon to them.
translations.idiomatic: " He tossed them his seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 吳人聽其辭而不取印綬。

translations.literal: The Wu men listened to his words but did not take the seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu accepted his story but did not take the seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 特乃投夜徹諸屋材柵，補其缺為二重，明日，謂吳人曰：「我但有斗死耳！

translations.literal: Te then in the night pulled down timber and palisades from the houses, repaired the gaps into a double line of defense, and the next day said to the Wu men: "I have only death in battle left!
translations.idiomatic: That night Te stripped timber and palisades from the houses and rebuilt the breaches into a double wall; the next day he told the Wu, "I have nothing left but to fight to the death!

sentences.zh: 」吳人大怒，進攻之，不能拔。

translations.literal: " The Wu were greatly enraged and pressed the attack, but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wu were furious and attacked again, but could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 會大暑，吳士疲勞，飲水，洩下，流腫，病者太半，死傷塗地。

translations.literal: It happened to be intense summer heat; the Wu soldiers were weary, drank water, suffered diarrhea and running sores, and more than half fell ill—dead and wounded covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Intense summer heat set in; the Wu troops, exhausted, drank foul water, suffered dysentery and sores, and more than half fell sick—dead and wounded littered the camp.

sentences.zh: 諸營吏日白病者多，恪以為詐，欲斬之，自是莫敢言。

translations.literal: The camp officers daily reported that the sick were many; Ke thought it deception and wished to execute them—from then on none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Camp officers daily reported heavy sickness; Ke called it deception and threatened execution—from then on none dared report the truth.

sentences.zh: 恪內惟失計，而恥城不下，忿形於色。

translations.literal: Within, Ke knew his plan had failed, yet was shamed that the city would not fall; his anger showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Ke knew inwardly that his strategy had failed, yet was ashamed that the city still held; his rage showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 將軍朱異以軍事迕恪，恪立奪其兵，斥還建業。

translations.literal: General Zhu Yi, because his military conduct crossed Ke, had his troops immediately seized by Ke and was sent back to Jianye in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhu Yi had crossed Ke over military matters; Ke immediately stripped him of command and sent him back to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 都尉蔡林數陳軍計，恪不能用，策馬來奔。

translations.literal: Commandant Cai Lin repeatedly set forth military plans; Ke could not use them and spurred his horse to come over in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Cai Lin repeatedly offered military advice that Ke ignored; he spurred his horse and defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 諸將伺知吳兵已疲，乃進救兵。

translations.literal: The various generals, observing that the Wu troops were already weary, then advanced with relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei generals, seeing that the Wu army was exhausted, advanced with relief troops.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，恪引軍去，士卒傷病，流曳道路，或頓僕坑壑，或見略獲，存亡哀痛，大小嗟呼。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Ke led the army away; the officers and men, wounded and sick, dragged themselves along the roads—some collapsing into ditches and ravines, some taken captive in raids—living and dead in grief and pain, young and old crying out.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Ke withdrew; wounded and sick soldiers straggled along the roads—some collapsing into ditches, some taken captive—dead and dying in anguish, men of every rank wailing.

sentences.zh: 而恪晏然自若，出住江渚一月，圖起田於潯陽；

translations.literal: Yet Ke was serene and at ease as before; he went out and stayed on the river islets for a month, planning to open fields at Xunyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ke remained serene and unperturbed, camping on the riverbanks for a month while planning to open farmland at Xunyang;

sentences.zh: 詔召相銜，徐乃旋師。

translations.literal: edicts summoning him came one after another, and only then did he slowly turn the army homeward.
translations.idiomatic: imperial summons came one after another before he slowly marched home.

sentences.zh: 由此眾庶失望，怨讟興矣。

translations.literal: From this the common people lost hope and resentment and slander arose.
translations.idiomatic: From this the people lost hope, and resentment and slander spread.

sentences.zh: 汝南太守鄧艾言於司馬師曰：「孫權已沒，大臣未附。

translations.literal: Runan Administrator Deng Ai said to Sima Shi: "Sun Quan is already dead and the great ministers are not yet attached.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai, Administrator of Runan, told Sima Shi, "Sun Quan is dead and the great ministers are not yet loyal.

sentences.zh: 吳名宗大族皆有部曲，阻兵仗勢，足以違命。

translations.literal: Wu’s eminent clans and great families all have private followings; they block the roads with arms and rely on their power—enough to defy orders.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s great clans all maintain private armies; armed and entrenched, they are strong enough to defy the throne.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪新秉國政，而內無其主，不念撫恤上下以立根基，競於外事，虐用其民，番國之眾，頓於堅城，死者萬數，載禍而歸，此恪獲罪之日也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke has newly grasped state power, yet within there is no true master; he does not think to comfort and succor superiors and subordinates to lay a foundation, but competes in foreign affairs and cruelly uses his people—the forces of a foreign state halted before a stout wall, tens of thousands dead, bearing calamity home in return: this is the day Ke will incur guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke has just seized power without a firm master at home; instead of winning hearts and building a foundation, he rushes into foreign wars and abuses his people—his army stalled before a stout wall, tens of thousands dead, returning in disaster: the day of his downfall is near.

sentences.zh: 昔子胥、吳起、商鞅、樂毅皆見任時君，主沒猶敗，況恪才非四賢，而不慮大患，其亡可待也。

translations.literal: In former times Wu Zixu, Wu Qi, Shang Yang, and Yue Yi were all employed by their lords of the time, yet when their lords died they still met defeat—how much more Ke, whose talent does not match the Four Worthies and who does not reckon with great peril: his destruction may be awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu, Wu Qi, Shang Yang, and Yue Yi all served their lords faithfully yet fell when their masters died—how much less can Ke, whose talent falls short of theirs and who ignores grave danger, hope to survive? His fall is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳軍還建業，諸葛恪陳兵導從，歸入府館，即召中書令孫嘿，厲聲謂曰：「卿等何敢數妄作詔！

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Wu army returned to Jianye; Zhuge Ke arrayed troops to escort him, entered his residence, and at once summoned Director of the Secretariat Sun He, saying in a harsh voice: "How dare you repeatedly issue false edicts!
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Wu army returned to Jianye; Zhuge Ke entered the city under military escort and immediately summoned Director of the Secretariat Sun He, demanding in a harsh voice, "How dare you repeatedly issue false edicts!

sentences.zh: 」嘿惶懼辭出，因病還家。

translations.literal: " He, in fear and trepidation, withdrew; citing illness, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun He withdrew in terror and retired home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 恪征行之後，曹所奏署令長職司，一罷更選，愈治威嚴，多所罪責，當進見者無不竦息。

translations.literal: After Ke’s campaign, all the magistrates and functionaries Cao had memorialized and appointed were dismissed and reselected; he governed with ever greater severity, imposed many punishments and blame, and none who were to come into audience failed to tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign Ke dismissed and replaced every magistrate Cao had appointed, ruled with growing severity, punished widely, and all who came to audience trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 又改易宿衛，用其親近；

translations.literal: He also changed the palace guard and used his intimates;
translations.idiomatic: He replaced the palace guard with his own men;

sentences.zh: 復敕兵嚴，欲向青、徐。

translations.literal: again ordered the troops to stand ready, intending to march toward Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: and again ordered the armies to prepare for a campaign against Qing and Xu.

sentences.zh: 孫峻因民之多怨，眾之所嫌，構恪於吳主，雲欲為變。

translations.literal: Sun Jun, relying on the people’s many grievances and the multitude’s dislike, framed Ke before the Wu ruler, saying he intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun, exploiting popular resentment, slandered Ke to the Wu emperor, claiming he planned a coup.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，孫峻與吳主謀置酒請恪。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Sun Jun and the Wu ruler plotted to set out wine and invite Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Sun Jun and the emperor plotted a banquet to lure Ke in.

sentences.zh: 恪將入之夜，精爽擾動，通夕不寐，又家數有妖怪，恪疑之。

translations.literal: On the night Ke was to enter, his spirit was disturbed; all night he did not sleep; moreover his household had several portents—Ke grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: On the night he was to attend, Ke was restless and sleepless; strange omens appeared in his household, and he grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 旦日，駐車宮門，峻已伏兵於帷中，恐恪不時入，事洩，乃自出見恪曰：「使君若尊體不安，自可須後，峻當具白主上。

translations.literal: At dawn he halted his carriage at the palace gate; Jun had already hidden troops behind the curtains, fearing Ke would not enter in time and the affair would leak out; he therefore came out himself to see Ke and said: "If your lordship’s honored person is unwell, you may naturally wait; Jun will fully report to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he halted at the palace gate; Jun had hidden troops behind the curtains and, fearing Ke might not come and the plot be exposed, went out to meet him: "If you are unwell, you may wait; I will report fully to His Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」欲以嘗知恪意。

translations.literal: " He wished thereby to test and learn Ke’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to sound Ke out.

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「當自力入。

translations.literal: Ke said: "I should exert myself and enter.
translations.idiomatic: Ke said, "I shall go in myself.

sentences.zh: 」散騎常侍張約、朱恩等密書與恪曰：「今日張設非常，疑有他故。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Zhang Yue, Zhu En, and others sent a secret letter to Ke, saying: "Today’s arrangements are extraordinary; we suspect some other cause.
translations.idiomatic: " Palace Attendants Zhang Yue and Zhu En sent Ke a secret note: "Today's arrangements are unusual; we suspect treachery.

sentences.zh: 」恪以書示滕胤，胤勸恪還。

translations.literal: " Ke showed the letter to Teng Yin; Yin urged Ke to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke showed the note to Teng Yin, who urged him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「兒輩何能為！

translations.literal: Ke said: "What can those boys do!
translations.idiomatic: Ke said, "What can those boys do to me!

sentences.zh: 正恐因酒食中人耳。

translations.literal: I only fear they may poison me through food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: I only fear poison in the food and wine.

sentences.zh: 」恪入，劍履上殿，進謝還坐。

translations.literal: Ke entered, wearing sword and shoes on the hall floor, advanced to give thanks and returned to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Ke entered, sword and shoes on the hall floor, offered thanks, and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 設酒，恪疑未飲。

translations.literal: Wine was set out; Ke was suspicious and did not drink.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was served; Ke suspected poison and would not drink.

sentences.zh: 孫峻曰：「使君病未善平，有常服藥酒，可取之。

translations.literal: Sun Jun said: "Your lordship’s illness is not yet fully settled; there is medicinal wine you regularly take—you may have it brought.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun said, "You are not yet fully recovered; here is your usual medicinal wine—you may drink it.

sentences.zh: 」恪意乃安。

translations.literal: " Ke’s mind was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke's suspicions eased.

sentences.zh: 別飲所繼酒，數行，吳主還內。

translations.literal: He drank separately the wine that followed; after several rounds the Wu ruler withdrew within.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the wine served afterward; after several rounds the emperor withdrew to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 峻起如廁，解長衣，著短服，出曰：「有詔收諸葛恪。

translations.literal: Jun rose as if to the privy, removed his long robe, put on short dress, came out and said: "There is an edict to seize Zhuge Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Jun rose as if for the privy, stripped off his long robe, put on fighting dress, and announced, "By imperial edict, seize Zhuge Ke!

sentences.zh: 」恪驚起，拔劍未得，而峻刀交下，張約從旁斫峻，裁傷左手，峻應手斫約，斷右臂。

translations.literal: " Ke started up in alarm, drew his sword but could not use it in time, while Jun’s blades struck down together; Zhang Yue hacked at Jun from the side and only wounded his left hand; Jun at once struck back at Yue and severed his right arm.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke sprang up in alarm but could not draw his sword in time; Jun's blades struck from every side; Zhang Yue hacked at Jun from the side and only wounded his left hand; Jun struck back and severed Yue's right arm.

sentences.zh: 武衛之士皆趨上殿，峻曰：「所取者恪也，今已死！

translations.literal: The martial guards all rushed onto the hall; Jun said: "The one sought is Ke, and he is already dead!
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards rushed onto the hall; Jun cried, "We sought only Ke, and he is already dead!

sentences.zh: 」悉令復刃，乃除地更飲。

translations.literal: " He ordered all to sheathe their blades, then cleared the ground and drank again.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered all blades sheathed, the floor cleared, and the banquet resumed.

sentences.zh: 恪二子竦、建聞難，載其母欲來奔，峻使人追殺之。

translations.literal: Ke’s two sons Song and Jian, hearing of the disaster, loaded their mother and wished to come flee; Jun sent men to pursue and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's sons Song and Jian, hearing of the attack, tried to flee with their mother; Jun sent men to pursue and kill them.

sentences.zh: 以葦席裹恪屍，篾束腰，投之石子岡。

translations.literal: They wrapped Ke’s corpse in a rush mat, bound the waist with bamboo strips, and cast it onto Shizi Hill.
translations.idiomatic: They wrapped Ke's corpse in a rush mat, bound it with bamboo strips, and cast it onto Shizi Hill.

sentences.zh: 又遣無難督施寬就將軍施績、孫壹軍，殺恪弟奮威將軍融於公安，及其三子。

translations.literal: He also sent Director of the Unconquered Shi Kuan to the armies of Generals Shi Ji and Sun Yi to kill Ke’s younger brother General Who Displays Might Rong at Gong'an, together with his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Director of the Unconquered Shi Kuan to the armies of Shi Ji and Sun Yi to kill Ke's brother Rong, General Who Displays Might, at Gong'an, along with his three sons.

sentences.zh: 恪外甥都鄉侯張震、常侍朱恩，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: Ke’s nephew Marquis of Duxiang Zhang Zhen and Regular Attendant Zhu En were both exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's nephew Zhang Zhen, Marquis of Duxiang, and Regular Attendant Zhu En were both exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 臨淮臧均表乞收葬恪曰：「震雷電激，不崇一朝；

translations.literal: Linhuai's Zang Jun memorialized begging permission to bury Ke, saying: "Thunder and lightning strike fiercely, yet do not last a whole morning;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Jun of Linhuai memorialized begging leave to bury Ke: "Thunder and lightning strike fiercely, yet do not last a whole morning;

sentences.zh: 大風沖發，希有極日；

translations.literal: great winds burst forth, rarely enduring a full day;
translations.idiomatic: great gales burst forth, rarely lasting a full day;

sentences.zh: 然猶繼之以雲雨，因以潤物。

translations.literal: yet still they are followed by clouds and rain, and thereby moisten the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: yet they are followed by clouds and rain that nourish the land.

sentences.zh: 是則天地之威，不可經日浹辰；

translations.literal: thus the majesty of Heaven and Earth cannot extend through a whole day and night;
translations.idiomatic: So the wrath of Heaven and Earth cannot endure even a day and night;

sentences.zh: 帝王之怒，不宜言乞情盡意。

translations.literal: the rage of emperors and kings should not be spoken of as begging for mercy to the full.
translations.idiomatic: the rage of emperors and kings should not be stretched to the uttermost.

sentences.zh: 臣以狂愚，不知忌諱，敢冒破滅之罪以邀風雨之會。

translations.literal: Your servant, in folly and ignorance, not knowing what is taboo, dares risk the crime of destruction to seek the season of wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, foolish and ignorant of propriety, dares risk destruction to plead for a season of mercy.

sentences.zh: 伏念故太傅諸葛恪，罪積惡盈，自致夷滅，父子三首，梟市積日，觀者數萬，詈聲成風；

translations.literal: I reflect that the late Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke, his crimes piled high and wickedness full, brought extermination on himself—father and sons, three heads exposed in the market for days on end, tens of thousands of onlookers, curses rising like the wind;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the late Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke, crimes piled high and wickedness overflowing, brought ruin on himself—father and sons, three heads exposed in the market for days, tens of thousands watching, curses rising like the wind;

sentences.zh: 國之大刑，無所不震，長老孩幼，無不畢見。

translations.literal: the great punishments of the state shake all without exception; elders and children alike have all witnessed it to the full.
translations.idiomatic: the state's supreme punishment has shaken all alike; young and old have witnessed it in full.

sentences.zh: 人情之於品物，樂極則哀生，見恪貴盛，世莫與貳，身處台輔，中間歷年，今之誅夷，無異禽獸，觀訖情反，能不憯然！

translations.literal: In human feeling toward things, when joy reaches its extreme sorrow is born; seeing Ke’s nobility and splendor, none in the age to match him, his person in the highest ministry for years in between—today’s execution and extermination no different from a beast’s: when the viewing is finished feelings turn, and one cannot but feel pity!
translations.idiomatic: Human nature turns from joy to sorrow at the extreme; Ke was once so glorious that none could rival him, holding the highest office for years—yet today's execution treats him no better than a beast; when the spectacle ends, hearts turn, and who cannot feel pity!

sentences.zh: 且已死之人，與土壤同域，鑿掘斫刺，無所復加。

translations.literal: Moreover one already dead shares the same realm as the soil—digging, hacking, and stabbing can add nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the dead share the earth with the soil—no digging or stabbing can add further harm.

sentences.zh: 願聖朝稽則乾坤，怒不極旬，使其鄉邑若故吏民收以士伍之服，惠以三寸之棺。

translations.literal: I wish the holy court, taking Heaven and Earth as its model, would not let anger reach the full ten days, but allow his native district and former subordinates and people to gather him in common soldier’s garb and favor him with a three-inch coffin.
translations.idiomatic: I pray the holy court, following the example of Heaven and Earth, will not let wrath endure ten full days, but allow his native district and former officers to bury him in commoner's garb with a simple coffin.

sentences.zh: 昔項籍受殯葬之施，韓信獲收斂之恩，斯則漢高發神明之譽也。

translations.literal: In former times Xiang Yu received the grace of burial rites and Han Xin obtained the kindness of proper interment—this was how Emperor Gaozu of Han won a reputation for divine wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu received burial rites and Han Xin was granted proper interment, Emperor Gaozu of Han won a reputation for divine magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下敦三皇之仁，垂哀矜之心，使國澤加於辜戮之骸，復受不已之恩，於以揚聲遐方，沮勸天下，豈不大哉！

translations.literal: May Your Majesty alone extend the benevolence of the Three Sovereigns, bestow a heart of pity and compassion, let the state’s grace fall on the bones of the guiltily slain, and grant unending favor—thereby spreading your renown to distant regions and discouraging and instructing all under Heaven: would this not be great!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty extend the benevolence of the Three Sovereigns, show pity and compassion, let state grace fall on the bones of the executed, and grant enduring mercy—thereby spreading your renown afar and instructing all under Heaven: would this not be magnificent!

sentences.zh: 昔欒布矯命彭越，臣竊恨之，不先請主上而專名以肆情，其得不誅，實為幸耳。

translations.literal: In former times Luan Bu forged orders for Peng Yue—I privately regret that he did not first ask his lord but acted on his own name to indulge his feelings; that he escaped execution was truly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan Bu forged orders to bury Peng Yue, he acted without asking his lord—I regret that I speak on my own authority; that I am not executed is itself good fortune.

sentences.zh: 今臣不敢章宣是表以露天恩，謹伏手書，冒昧陳聞，乞聖明哀察。

translations.literal: Now your servant dares not proclaim this memorial openly to display Heaven’s grace; I respectfully submit this handwritten letter, rashly stating my plea, begging the sage clarity to pity and examine it.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not proclaim this memorial openly; I respectfully submit this private letter, rashly stating my plea, and beg Your Sage Majesty's pity and consideration.

sentences.zh: 」於是吳主及孫峻聽恪故吏斂葬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Wu ruler and Sun Jun permitted Ke’s former subordinates to gather and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Wu emperor and Sun Jun allowed Ke's former officers to bury him.

sentences.zh: 初，恪少有盛名，大帝深器重之，而恪父瑾常以為戚，曰：「非保家之主也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ke in youth had great renown; the Great Emperor deeply valued him, yet Ke’s father Jin often took this as a sorrow, saying: "He is not one who can preserve the family.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ke had won great fame in youth, and the Great Emperor valued him highly, yet his father Jin often grieved, saying, "He is not a man who can preserve the family line.

sentences.zh: 」父友奮威將軍張承亦以為恪必敗諸葛氏。

translations.literal: " His father’s friend General Who Displays Might Zhang Cheng also held that Ke would surely ruin the Zhuge clan.
translations.idiomatic: " His father's friend Zhang Cheng, General Who Displays Might, also believed Ke would ruin the Zhuge clan.

sentences.zh: 陸遜嘗謂恪曰：「在我前者吾必奉之同升，在我下者則扶接之；

translations.literal: Lu Xun once said to Ke: "Those before me I must surely honor and rise with together; those below me I must support and receive;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun once told Ke, "Those above me I must honor and rise with; those below me I must support and lift up;

sentences.zh: 今觀君氣陵其上，意蔑乎下，非安德之基也。

translations.literal: now observing you, your spirit overtops those above and your mind despises those below—this is not the foundation of secure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: but I see your spirit overbearing toward superiors and contemptuous toward inferiors—this is no foundation for lasting virtue.

sentences.zh: 」漢侍中諸葛瞻，亮之子也；

translations.literal: " Shu’s Palace Attendant Zhuge Zhan was Liang’s son;
translations.idiomatic: " In Shu, Palace Attendant Zhuge Zhan was Zhuge Liang's son;

sentences.zh: 恪再攻淮南，越巂太守張嶷與瞻書曰：「東主初崩，帝實幼弱，太傅受寄托之重，亦何容易！

translations.literal: when Ke again attacked Huainan, Yuexi Administrator Zhang Ni wrote to Zhan, saying: "The eastern lord has just died, the emperor is truly young and weak, and the Grand Tutor bears the weight of a deathbed trust—how can this be easy!
translations.idiomatic: when Ke again attacked Huainan, Zhang Ni of Yuexi wrote to Zhan: "The eastern lord has just died, the emperor is young and weak, and the Grand Tutor bears a deathbed trust—how perilous this is!

sentences.zh: 親有周公之才，猶有管、蔡流言之變，霍光受任，亦有燕、蓋、上官逆亂之謀，賴成、昭之明以免斯難耳。

translations.literal: Even with the Duke of Zhou’s talent at hand, there were still the slanderous troubles of Guan and Cai; when Huo Guang received his charge, there were also the rebellious plots of Yan, Gai, and Shangguan—only through the clarity of Cheng and Zhao were such perils avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou faced the slanders of Guan and Cai; Huo Guang faced plots from Yan, Gai, and Shangguan—only the wisdom of Emperor Cheng and Emperor Zhao averted disaster.

sentences.zh: 昔每聞東主殺生賞罰，不任下人，又今以垂沒之命，卒召太傅，屬以後事，誠實可慮。

translations.literal: In former times I often heard that the eastern lord in life and death, rewards and punishments, did not entrust subordinates; and now, on his dying command, he suddenly summoned the Grand Tutor and entrusted him with later affairs—this is truly cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: I have long heard that the eastern lord kept life-and-death power in his own hands; now, on his deathbed, he suddenly summoned the Grand Tutor and entrusted him with the realm—this is truly worrisome.

sentences.zh: 加吳楚剽急，乃昔所記，而太傅離少主，履敵庭，恐非良計長算也。

translations.literal: Moreover Wu and Chu are swift and fierce, as recorded of old; yet the Grand Tutor leaves the young lord and treads the enemy’s court—I fear this is not a good plan or long calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wu and Chu are fierce peoples of old renown; for the Grand Tutor to leave the young sovereign and tread enemy territory is hardly wise long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 雖雲東家綱紀肅然，上下輯睦；

translations.literal: Although it is said the eastern house’s discipline is stern and superiors and subordinates are harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: Though it is said the eastern court is well ordered and harmonious;

sentences.zh: 百有一失，非明者之慮也。

translations.literal: in a hundred there is one lapse—this is not what the clear-sighted should reckon on.
translations.idiomatic: in a hundred cases there is one lapse—not what the wise should rely upon.

sentences.zh: 取古則今，今則古也，自非郎君進忠言於太傅，誰復有盡言者邪！

translations.literal: Take the past as measure for the present, and the present becomes the past; unless you, sir, advance loyal words to the Grand Tutor, who else will speak fully!
translations.idiomatic: The past illuminates the present; unless you, sir, offer loyal counsel to the Grand Tutor, who else will speak plainly!

sentences.zh: 旋軍廣農，務行德惠，數年之中，東西並舉，實為不晚，願深采察！

translations.literal: Turn the army, extend agriculture, devote yourself to virtue and kindness; within a few years, striking east and west together would truly not be late—I beg you to examine this deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw the armies, promote agriculture, and practice benevolence; within a few years a campaign on both fronts would not be too late—I beg you to consider this carefully!

sentences.zh: 」恪果以此敗。

translations.literal: " Ke indeed met defeat for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke was indeed ruined for just these reasons.

sentences.zh: 吳群臣共議上奏，推孫峻為太尉，滕胤為司徒。

translations.literal: The Wu ministers jointly deliberated and memorialized, recommending Sun Jun as Grand Commandant and Teng Yin as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ministers jointly memorialized, recommending Sun Jun as Grand Commandant and Teng Yin as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 有媚峻者言曰：「萬機宜在公族，若承嗣為亞公，聲名素重，眾心所附，不可量也。

translations.literal: One who flattered Jun said: "The myriad affairs of state should rest with the ducal clan; if Chengsi became second minister, his fame is weighty of old and the people's hearts attach to him—he cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: A flatterer of Jun said, "State affairs should rest with the imperial clan; if Teng Yin became second minister, his long-standing fame and popular support would make him impossible to measure.

sentences.zh: 」乃表峻為丞相、大將軍，督中外諸軍事，又不置御史大夫；

translations.literal: " Thereupon they memorialized Jun as Chancellor and Grand General, supervisor of all military affairs at home and abroad, and did not appoint a Grand Censor;
translations.idiomatic: " They then memorialized Jun as Chancellor and Grand General with supreme military command, and did not appoint a Grand Censor;

sentences.zh: 由是士人失望。

translations.literal: from this the scholar-officials were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: from this the scholar-officials were deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 滕胤女為恪子竦妻，胤以此辭位。

translations.literal: Teng Yin’s daughter was wife to Ke’s son Song; Yin for this reason declined office.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin's daughter had been married to Ke's son Song; Yin declined office for this reason.

sentences.zh: 孫峻曰：「鯀、禹罪不相及，滕侯何為！

translations.literal: Sun Jun said: "Gun and Yu’s crimes did not reach each other—what is Marquis Teng doing!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun said, "Gun and Yu were not punished for each other's crimes—why should Marquis Teng decline!

sentences.zh: 」峻與胤雖內不沾洽，而外相苞容，進胤爵高密侯，共事如前。

translations.literal: " Though Jun and Yin were not harmonious within, outwardly they accommodated each other; Jun advanced Yin’s noble rank to Marquis of Gaomi, and they worked together as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Though Jun and Yin were not close inwardly, outwardly they accommodated each other; Jun advanced Yin to Marquis of Gaomi, and they worked together as before.

sentences.zh: 齊王奮聞諸葛恪誅，下住蕪湖，欲至建業觀變。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Fen, hearing of Zhuge Ke’s execution, came down and stayed at Wuhu, wishing to go to Jianye to observe the turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fen of Qi, hearing of Zhuge Ke's execution, moved down to Wuhu, intending to go to Jianye to watch how events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 傅相謝慈等諫，奮殺之，坐廢為庶人，徙章安。

translations.literal: Tutor Xie Ci and others remonstrated; Fen killed them and for this was demoted to commoner and moved to Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His tutor Xie Ci and others remonstrated; Fen killed them and was demoted to commoner status and exiled to Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 南陽王和妃張氏，諸葛恪之甥也。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang He’s consort Lady Zhang was Zhuge Ke’s niece.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, consort of Prince He of Nanyang, was Zhuge Ke's niece.

sentences.zh: 先是恪有徙都之意，使治武昌宮，民間或言恪欲迎和立之。

translations.literal: Earlier Ke had intended to move the capital and had the Wuchang palace repaired; among the people some said Ke wished to welcome He and establish him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ke had planned to move the capital and had the Wuchang palace repaired; rumor held that Ke meant to install Prince He on the throne.

sentences.zh: 及恪被誅，丞相峻因此奪和璽綬，徙新都，又遣使者追賜死。

translations.literal: When Ke was executed, Chancellor Jun for this reason seized He’s seal and ribbon, moved him to the new capital, and also sent envoys in pursuit to grant him death.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke was executed, Chancellor Jun seized He's seal and ribbon, moved him to the new capital, and sent envoys to order his death.

sentences.zh: 初，和妾何氏生子皓，諸姬子德、謙、俊。

translations.literal: Earlier, He’s concubine Lady He bore son Hao; the various consorts bore sons De, Qian, and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince He had a concubine, Lady He, who bore son Hao; other consorts bore sons De, Qian, and Jun.

sentences.zh: 和將死，與張妃別，妃曰：「吉凶當相隨，終不獨生。

translations.literal: As He was about to die, he took leave of Consort Zhang; the consort said: "Fortune and misfortune should be followed together—I will never live alone.
translations.idiomatic: As He faced death, he bade farewell to Consort Zhang; she said, "In fortune or misfortune we should go together—I will not live alone.

sentences.zh: 」亦自殺。

translations.literal: " She too killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She too took her own life.

sentences.zh: 何姬曰：「若皆從死，誰當字孤！

translations.literal: Lady He said: "If all follow in death, who will nurture the orphans!
translations.idiomatic: Lady He said, "If all die, who will raise the orphans!

sentences.zh: 」遂撫育皓及其三弟，皆賴以獲全。

translations.literal: " She thereupon reared Hao and his three younger brothers, and all relied on her to be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: " She then raised Hao and his three brothers, and all were preserved through her care.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公上

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公下正元元年（

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Duke of Shaoling, first year of Zhengyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Duke of Shaoling, first year of Zhengyuan (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元二五四年）

translations.literal: jiaxu, AD 254)
translations.idiomatic: the year jiaxu, AD 254)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，殺中書令李豐。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Director of the Secretariat Li Feng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, Director of the Secretariat Li Feng was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，豐年十七、八，已有清名，海內翕然稱之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Feng was seventeen or eighteen, he already had a pure reputation; within the seas all harmoniously praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Feng was seventeen or eighteen, he already enjoyed a spotless reputation; all under Heaven spoke of him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 其父太僕恢不願其然，敕使閉門斷客。

translations.literal: His father, Minister of Coaches Hui, did not wish this and ordered him to shut the gate and cut off visitors.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, Minister of Coaches, disapproved and ordered him to shut his gate and refuse visitors.

sentences.zh: 曹爽專政，司馬懿稱疾不出，豐為尚書僕射，依違二公間，故不與爽同誅。

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang monopolized government and Sima Yi claimed illness and did not emerge, Feng was Vice Director of the Secretariat, wavering between the two lords, and therefore was not executed with Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang monopolized power and Sima Yi feigned illness and held aloof, Feng served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, steering between the two factions, and thus escaped execution with Shuang.

sentences.zh: 豐子韜，以選尚齊長公主。

translations.literal: Feng’s son Tao, by selection, married the Princess of Qi the elder.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son Tao was selected to marry the Elder Princess of Qi.

sentences.zh: 司馬師秉政，以豐為中書令。

translations.literal: When Sima Shi held government, Feng was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Shi took power, Feng was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，太常夏侯玄有天下重名，以曹爽親故，不得在勢任，居常怏怏；

translations.literal: At this time Grand Commandant of Ceremonies Xiahou Xuan had a weighty reputation throughout the realm; because he was kin to Cao Shuang he could not hold power and office, and was habitually discontent;
translations.idiomatic: At this time Xiahou Xuan, Grand Commandant of Ceremonies, enjoyed a towering reputation; as a kinsman of Cao Shuang he held no real power and was habitually discontent;

sentences.zh: 張緝以後父去郡家居，亦不得意。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, as empress’s father, had left his commandery and lived at home, and was also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, as father of the empress, had left office and lived at home, and was likewise discontent.

sentences.zh: 豐皆與之親善。

translations.literal: Feng was on intimate and friendly terms with both.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was on intimate terms with both men.

sentences.zh: 師雖擢用豐，豐私心常在玄。

translations.literal: Although Shi promoted and employed Feng, Feng’s private heart always remained with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shi promoted Feng, Feng's loyalty remained with Xiahou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 豐在中書二歲，帝數獨召豐與語，不知所說。

translations.literal: Feng was in the Secretariat for two years; the emperor repeatedly summoned Feng alone to speak with him—what was said was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: For two years Feng served in the Secretariat; the emperor repeatedly summoned him for private talks—no one knew what was said.

sentences.zh: 師知其議己，請豐相見以詰豐，豐不以實告；

translations.literal: Shi knew they were plotting against him and asked to meet Feng to interrogate him; Feng did not tell the truth;
translations.idiomatic: Shi learned they were plotting against him and summoned Feng to question him; Feng would not confess;

sentences.zh: 師怒，以刀鐶築殺之，送屍付廷尉，遂收豐子韜及夏侯玄、張緝等皆下廷尉，鐘毓案治，云：「豐與黃門監蘇鑠，永寧署令樂敦，冗從僕射劉賢等謀曰：『拜貴人日，諸營兵皆屯門，陛下臨軒，因此同奉陛下，將群僚人兵，就誅大將軍；

translations.literal: Shi in anger killed him with the ring of a sword-hilt, sent the corpse to the Minister of Justice, and then arrested Feng’s son Tao and Xiahou Xuan, Zhang Ji, and the rest, all sent down to the Minister of Justice; Zhong Yu investigated the case, saying: "Feng with Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Yongning Office Director Yue Dun, Supernumerary Attendant Liu Xian, and others plotted, saying: 'On the day of investing the honored lady, all camp troops shall mass at the gates; when His Majesty appears at the hall, thereby together we shall support His Majesty, take the various officials’ men and troops, and go to execute the Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: Shi in fury beat him to death with a sword-ring, sent the body to the Minister of Justice, and arrested Feng's son Tao, Xiahou Xuan, Zhang Ji, and the rest; Zhong Yu investigated and reported: "Feng plotted with Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Yongning Office Director Yue Dun, Supernumerary Attendant Liu Xian, and others, saying, 'On the day the consort is invested, mass the camp troops at the gates; when His Majesty appears at the hall, we shall together support him, rally the officials' troops, and execute the Grand General;

sentences.zh: 陛下儻不從人，便當劫將去耳。

translations.literal: if His Majesty perchance does not follow the people, then we shall seize the general and take him away.'
translations.idiomatic: if His Majesty refuses, we shall seize the general and carry him off.'

sentences.zh: 』」又云：「謀以玄為大將軍，緝為驃騎將軍；

translations.literal: '" He also said: "They plotted to make Xuan Grand General and Ji General of Agile Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: " He also reported, "They planned to make Xuan Grand General and Ji General of Agile Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 玄、緝皆知其謀。

translations.literal: Xuan and Ji both knew of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Ji both knew of the plot.

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，誅韜、玄、緝、鑠、敦、賢，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: " On gengxu, Tao, Xuan, Ji, Shuo, Dun, and Xian were executed, all exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day gengxu, Tao, Xuan, Ji, Shuo, Dun, and Xian were executed and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 夏侯霸之入蜀也，邀玄欲與之俱，玄不從。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Ba entered Shu, he invited Xuan to go with him; Xuan would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Ba fled to Shu, he invited Xuan to join him; Xuan refused.

sentences.zh: 及司馬懿薨，中領軍高陽許允謂玄曰：「無復憂矣！

translations.literal: When Sima Yi died, Central Army Commander Gaoyang Xu Yun said to Xuan: "There is nothing more to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi died, Central Army Commander Xu Yun of Gaoyang told Xuan, "You need worry no more!

sentences.zh: 」玄歎曰：「士宗，卿何不見事乎！

translations.literal: " Xuan sighed and said: "Shizong, why do you not see how things stand!
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan sighed, "Shizong, why do you not see how things stand!

sentences.zh: 此人猶能以通家年少遇我，子元、子上不吾容也。

translations.literal: This man could still treat me generously as a young man of allied families; Ziyuan and Zishang will not tolerate me.
translations.idiomatic: This man still treated me generously as a family friend; Ziyuan and Zishang will not spare me.

sentences.zh: 」及下獄，玄不肯下辭，鍾毓自臨治之。

translations.literal: " When he was cast into prison, Xuan would not submit a confession; Zhong Yu personally came to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: " When imprisoned, Xuan refused to confess; Zhong Yu came to try him in person.

sentences.zh: 玄正色責毓曰：「吾當何罪！

translations.literal: Xuan with stern countenance reproached Yu, saying: "What crime have I committed!
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sternly reproached Yu: "What crime have I committed!

sentences.zh: 卿為令史責人也，卿便為吾作！

translations.literal: You are a clerk charged with blaming men—then you write it for me!
translations.idiomatic: You are a clerk whose job is to assign blame—then write it for me!

sentences.zh: 」毓以玄名士，節高，不可屈，而獄當竟，夜為作辭，令與事相附，流涕以示玄；

translations.literal: " Yu, considering Xuan a famous gentleman of lofty integrity who could not be bent, yet that the case must be concluded, at night composed a confession for him, made it fit the affair, and with tears showed it to Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: " Yu knew Xuan was a famous gentleman of unbending integrity, yet the case had to close; at night he drafted a confession fitting the charges and, weeping, showed it to Xuan;

sentences.zh: 玄視，頷之而已。

translations.literal: Xuan looked at it and merely nodded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan looked at it and merely nodded.

sentences.zh: 及就東市，顏色不變，舉動自若。

translations.literal: When he went to the eastern market, his complexion did not change and his bearing remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When led to the eastern market, his color did not change and his bearing remained composed.

sentences.zh: 李豐弟翼，為兗州刺史，司馬師遣使收之。

translations.literal: Li Feng’s younger brother Yi was Inspector of Yanzhou; Sima Shi sent envoys to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng's younger brother Yi, Inspector of Yanzhou, was seized by envoys from Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 翼妻荀氏謂翼曰：「中書事發，可及詔書未至赴吳，何為坐取死亡！

translations.literal: Yi’s wife Lady Xun said to Yi: "The Secretariat affair has broken out—you can reach Wu before the edict arrives; why sit here and invite death!
translations.idiomatic: Yi's wife Lady Xun told him, "The Secretariat plot has been exposed—you can reach Wu before the arrest order arrives; why sit here and wait for death!

sentences.zh: 左右可共同赴水火者為誰？

translations.literal: Who among those around you can together go through fire and water with you?
translations.idiomatic: Who among your followers would go through fire and water with you?

sentences.zh: 」翼思未答，妻曰：「君在大州，不知可與同死生者，雖去亦不免！

translations.literal: " Yi thought but did not answer; his wife said: "You hold a great province yet do not know who would live or die with you—even if you flee you cannot escape!
translations.idiomatic: " Yi hesitated; his wife said, "You command a great province yet do not know who would die with you—even flight will not save you!

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「二兒小，吾不去，今但從坐身死耳，二兒必免。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The two boys are small; I will not go. Now I shall only die for association by law—the two boys will surely be spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "My two sons are young; I will not flee. I shall die for association, but the boys will be spared.

sentences.zh: 」乃止，死。

translations.literal: " He thereupon stopped, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He stayed, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，李恢與尚書僕射杜畿及東安太守郭智善，智子沖，有內實而無外觀，州裡弗稱也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Hui was on good terms with Vice Director of the Secretariat Du Ji and Dong'an Administrator Guo Zhi; Zhi’s son Chong had inner substance but no outward show, and the district did not praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Hui was friendly with Vice Director Du Ji and Dong'an Administrator Guo Zhi; Zhi's son Chong had substance but no outward brilliance, and locals did not praise him.

sentences.zh: 沖嘗與李豐俱見畿，既退，畿歎曰：「孝懿無子；

translations.literal: Chong once went with Li Feng together to see Ji; after they withdrew, Ji sighed and said: "Xiaoyi has no [worthy] son;
translations.idiomatic: Chong once visited Ji with Li Feng; after they left, Ji sighed, "Xiaoyi has no worthy son;

sentences.zh: 非徒無子，殆將無家。

translations.literal: not only no son—he will likely have no family left.
translations.idiomatic: not only no son—he will likely destroy his whole family.

sentences.zh: 君謀為不死也，其子足繼其業。

translations.literal: You, sir, plot not to die; your son is enough to carry on your enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, seek to survive; your son is fit to carry on your work.

sentences.zh: 」時人皆以畿為誤。

translations.literal: " People of the time all thought Ji was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time everyone thought Ji was wrong.

sentences.zh: 及豐死，沖為代君太守，卒繼父業。

translations.literal: When Feng died, Chong became Administrator of Daijun and in the end succeeded to his father’s work.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng died, Chong became Administrator of Daijun and eventually succeeded his father.

sentences.zh: 正始中，夏侯玄、何晏、鄧颺俱有盛名，欲交尚書郎傅嘏，嘏不受。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, Xiahou Xuan, He Yan, and Deng Yang all had great fame and wished to befriend Secretariat Gentleman Fu Gu; Gu would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era Xiahou Xuan, He Yan, and Deng Yang were all famous and sought friendship with Secretariat Gentleman Fu Gu; Gu refused.

sentences.zh: 嘏友人荀粲怪而問之，嘏曰：「太初志大其量，能合虛聲而無實才。

translations.literal: Gu’s friend Xun Can wondered at this and asked him; Gu said: "Taichu’s ambition exceeds his capacity; he can gather empty reputation but has no real talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's friend Xun Can asked why; Gu replied, "Taichu's ambition exceeds his ability; he gathers empty reputation but lacks real talent.

sentences.zh: 何平叔言遠而情近，好辯而無誠，所謂利口覆邦國之人也。

translations.literal: He Pingshu speaks far yet his feelings are near, loves disputation yet has no sincerity—the sort called sharp-tongued destroyers of states.
translations.idiomatic: He Pingshu speaks loftily yet thinks narrowly, loves debate but lacks sincerity—a sharp tongue that can overturn a state.

sentences.zh: 鄧玄茂有為而無終，外要名利，內無關鑰，貴同惡異，多言而妒前；

translations.literal: Deng Xuanmao acts but does not finish; outwardly he seeks fame and profit, inwardly he has no key to hold things; he honors sameness and hates difference, talks much and envies those before him;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xuanmao acts but never finishes; outwardly he craves fame, inwardly he lacks substance; he favors allies and hates dissent, talks much and envies his betters;

sentences.zh: 多言多釁，妒前無親。

translations.literal: much talk brings many troubles; envy of those before leaves no intimates.
translations.idiomatic: much talk breeds trouble; envy of betters wins no friends.

sentences.zh: 以吾觀此三人者，皆將敗家；

translations.literal: in my view these three men will all ruin their families;
translations.idiomatic: in my view all three will ruin their families;

sentences.zh: 遠之猶恐禍及，況暱之乎！

translations.literal: to keep distant from them one still fears calamity may reach one—how much more to draw close to them!
translations.idiomatic: to keep one's distance still risks calamity—how much more to befriend them!

sentences.zh: 」嘏又與李豐不善，謂同志曰：「豐飾偽而多疑，矜小智而昧於權利，若任機事，其死必矣！

translations.literal: " Gu was also not on good terms with Li Feng and said to his comrades: "Feng adorns himself with falsehood and is much suspicious, prides himself on small cleverness yet is blind to power and profit—if entrusted with critical affairs, he is sure to die!
translations.idiomatic: " Gu also disliked Li Feng and told his friends, "Feng is false and suspicious, prides himself on petty cleverness yet is blind to power—entrust him with critical affairs and he is sure to die!

sentences.zh: 辛亥，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinhai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 三月，廢皇后張氏，夏，四月，立皇后王氏，奉車都尉夔之女也。

translations.literal: In the third month, Empress Zhang was deposed; in summer, the fourth month, Empress Wang was established—daughter of Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Kui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Empress Zhang was deposed; in summer, the fourth month, Empress Wang was installed—daughter of Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Kui.

sentences.zh: 狄道長李簡密書請降於漢。

translations.literal: Didao Chief Li Jian by secret letter asked to surrender to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian, chief of Didao, sent a secret letter offering surrender to Shu.

sentences.zh: 六月，姜維寇隴西。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Jiang Wei raided Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jiang Wei raided Longxi.

sentences.zh: 中領軍許允素與李豐、夏侯玄善。

translations.literal: Central Army Commander Xu Yun had long been on good terms with Li Feng and Xiahou Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Commander Xu Yun had long been close to Li Feng and Xiahou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 秋，允為鎮北將軍、假節、都督河北諸軍事。

translations.literal: In autumn, Yun was made General Who Guards the North, with provisional staff of authority and command over all military affairs north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Yun was appointed General Who Guards the North, with staff of authority and command over all forces north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 帝以允當出，詔會群臣，帝特引允以自近；

translations.literal: because Yun was about to depart, the emperor ordered the ministers to assemble and specially drew Yun close to himself;
translations.idiomatic: as Yun was to depart, the emperor summoned the ministers and drew Yun especially close;

sentences.zh: 允當與帝別，涕泣歔欷。
