translations.literal: when Yun was to take leave of the emperor, they wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: when Yun took leave of the emperor, both wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 允未發，有司奏允前放散官物，收付廷尉，徙樂浪，未至，道死。

translations.literal: Before Yun had set out, the responsible offices memorialized that Yun had earlier distributed official goods; he was seized and handed to the Minister of Justice, exiled to Lelang, and before he arrived died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yun departed, officials reported that he had earlier distributed state property; he was arrested, handed to the Minister of Justice, exiled to Lelang, and died on the road before arriving.

sentences.zh: 吳孫峻驕矜淫暴，國人側目。

translations.literal: In Wu, Sun Jun was arrogant, proud, dissolute, and cruel; the people of the state looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Sun Jun was arrogant, dissolute, and cruel; the people glared at him in anger.

sentences.zh: 司馬桓慮謀殺峻，立太子登之子吳侯英；

translations.literal: Sima Huan Lü plotted to kill Jun and establish Crown Prince Deng’s son Marquis of Wu Ying;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Huan Lü plotted to kill Jun and install Crown Prince Deng's son, Marquis Ying of Wu;

sentences.zh: 不克，皆死。

translations.literal: they did not succeed and all died.
translations.idiomatic: the plot failed and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 帝以李豐之死，意殊不平。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of Li Feng’s death, was especially displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased over Li Feng's death.

sentences.zh: 安東將軍司馬昭鎮許昌，詔召之使擊姜維。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the East Sima Zhao was stationed at Xuchang; an edict summoned him to attack Jiang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the East Sima Zhao was stationed at Xuchang; an edict summoned him to attack Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 九月，昭領兵入見，帝幸平樂觀以臨軍過。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhao led his troops in to audience; the emperor went to Pingle Terrace to oversee the army’s passage.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhao marched in to audience; the emperor went to Pingle Terrace to review the troops.

sentences.zh: 左右勸帝因昭辭，殺之，勒兵以退大將軍；

translations.literal: those around him urged the emperor, when Zhao took leave, to kill him and command the troops to drive back the Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: his attendants urged the emperor to kill Zhao when he took leave and use the troops to drive back the Grand General;

sentences.zh: 已書詔於前，帝懼，不敢發。

translations.literal: the edict had already been written before him, but the emperor in fear did not dare issue it.
translations.idiomatic: the edict was already written, but the emperor in fear did not dare issue it.

sentences.zh: 昭引兵入城，大將軍師乃謀廢帝。

translations.literal: Zhao led his troops into the city; Grand General Shi thereupon plotted to depose the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao led his troops into the capital; Grand General Shi then plotted to depose the emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，師以皇太后令召群臣會議，以帝荒淫無度，褻近倡優，不可以承天緒；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Shi by the empress dowager’s order summoned the ministers to council, on the grounds that the emperor was dissolute beyond measure, intimate with actors and jesters, and could not undertake the imperial succession;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Shi summoned the ministers by the empress dowager's order, declaring the emperor dissolute beyond measure, intimate with actors and jesters, unfit to hold the throne;

sentences.zh: 群臣皆莫敢違。

translations.literal: none of the ministers dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: none of the ministers dared object.

sentences.zh: 乃奏收帝璽綬，歸籓於齊。

translations.literal: They then memorialized to take the emperor’s seal and ribbon and return him to his fief as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized to seize the imperial seal and ribbon and reduce him to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 使郭芝入白太后，太后方與帝對坐，芝謂帝曰：「大將軍欲廢陛下，立彭城王據！

translations.literal: He sent Guo Zhi in to inform the empress dowager; the dowager was just then sitting opposite the emperor; Zhi said to the emperor: "The Grand General wishes to depose Your Majesty and establish Prince of Pengcheng Ju!
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guo Zhi to inform the empress dowager; she was sitting opposite the emperor; Zhi told the emperor, "The Grand General wishes to depose you and install Prince Ju of Pengcheng!

sentences.zh: 」帝乃起去。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon rose and left.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor rose and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太后不悅。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was displeased.

sentences.zh: 芝曰：「太后有子不能教，今大將軍意已成，又勒兵於外以備非常，但當順旨，將復何言！

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Your Majesty had a son yet could not instruct him; now the Grand General’s intent is already fixed, and he has moreover mustered troops outside to guard against the unexpected—you should only follow his will; what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "You had a son yet could not instruct him; the Grand General's mind is made up and troops are mustered outside against any surprise—you must obey; what more is there to say!

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「我欲見大將軍，口有所說。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager said: "I wish to see the Grand General; I have something to say.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager said, "I wish to see the Grand General; I have something to say.

sentences.zh: 」芝曰：「何可見邪！

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "How could you see him!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi said, "That is impossible!

sentences.zh: 但當速取璽綬！

translations.literal: You should only quickly take the seal and ribbon!
translations.idiomatic: You must quickly surrender the seal and ribbon!

sentences.zh: 」太后意折，乃遣傍侍御取璽綬著坐側。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager’s will was broken; she then sent a nearby attendant to take the seal and ribbon and place them beside her seat.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager's will broke; she sent an attendant to fetch the seal and ribbon and place them beside her.

sentences.zh: 芝出報師，師甚喜。

translations.literal: Zhi went out and reported to Shi; Shi was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi reported to Shi, who was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 又遣使者授帝齊王印綬，使出就西宮。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to bestow on the emperor the Prince of Qi’s seal and ribbon and have him go out to the western palace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to give the emperor the seal and ribbon of Prince of Qi and send him to the western palace.

sentences.zh: 帝與太后垂涕而別，遂乘王車，從太極殿南出，群臣送者數十人，司馬孚悲不自勝，餘多流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor and the empress dowager parted with tears falling; he then rode the prince’s carriage and went out south from the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; several tens of ministers who saw him off—Sima Fu in grief beyond control, the rest mostly in tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress dowager parted in tears; he rode the prince's carriage out south from the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; several dozen ministers saw him off—Sima Fu was overcome with grief, most others weeping.

sentences.zh: 師又使使者請璽綬於太后。

translations.literal: Shi again sent envoys to request the seal and ribbon from the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Shi again sent envoys to request the seal and ribbon from the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「彭城王，我之季叔也，今來立，我當何之！

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "The Prince of Pengcheng is my youngest uncle-by-marriage; if he comes now to be established, where am I to go!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Prince Ju of Pengcheng is my husband's youngest uncle; if he is installed, where am I to go!

sentences.zh: 且明皇帝當永絕嗣乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, is Emperor Ming to be cut off forever from heirs?
translations.idiomatic: And is Emperor Ming to be cut off forever from heirs?

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公，文皇帝之長孫，明皇帝之弟子。

translations.literal: The Duke of Gaoguixiang is Emperor Wen’s eldest grandson and Emperor Ming’s younger brother’s son.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Gaoguixiang is Emperor Wen's eldest grandson and Emperor Ming's nephew.

sentences.zh: 於禮，小宗有後大宗之義，其詳議之。

translations.literal: By ritual, the lesser lineage may continue the greater lineage—let this be deliberated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual law the lesser line may continue the greater—let this be deliberated in full.

sentences.zh: 」丁丑，師更召群臣，以太后令示之，乃定迎高貴鄉公髦於元城。

translations.literal: " On dingchou, Shi again summoned the ministers, showed them the empress dowager’s order, and thereupon decided to welcome the Duke of Gaoguixiang Mao from Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day dingchou, Shi summoned the ministers again, showed them the empress dowager's order, and decided to welcome the Duke of Gaoguixiang, Mao, from Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 髦者，東海定王霖之子也，時年十四，使太常王肅持節迎之。

translations.literal: Mao was son of Prince of Donghai Ding Wang Lin; he was then fourteen; Grand Commandant of Ceremonies Wang Su was sent with staff of authority to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was the son of Prince Lin of Donghai; he was fourteen; Grand Commandant of Ceremonies Wang Su was sent with staff of authority to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 師又使請璽綬，太后曰：「我見高貴鄉公，小時識之，我自欲以璽綬手授之。

translations.literal: Shi again sent to request the seal and ribbon; the empress dowager said: "I have seen the Duke of Gaoguixiang and knew him as a child; I myself wish to hand him the seal and ribbon in person.
translations.idiomatic: Shi again requested the seal and ribbon; the empress dowager said, "I knew the Duke of Gaoguixiang as a child; I wish to hand him the seal and ribbon myself.

sentences.zh: 」冬，十月，己丑，高貴鄉公至玄武館，群臣奏請捨前殿，公以先帝舊處，避止西廂；

translations.literal: " In winter, the tenth month, on jichou, the Duke of Gaoguixiang arrived at the Xuanwu Lodge; the ministers memorialized asking him to leave the front hall; the duke, because it was the late emperor’s former place, avoided it and stopped in the western wing;
translations.idiomatic: " In winter, the tenth month, on the day jichou, the Duke of Gaoguixiang arrived at the Xuanwu Lodge; the ministers asked him to occupy the front hall; he declined, as it was the late emperor's former quarters, and stayed in the western wing;

sentences.zh: 群臣又請以法駕迎，公不聽。

translations.literal: the ministers again asked to welcome him with the imperial carriage; the duke would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers again asked to welcome him with the imperial carriage; he refused.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公入於洛陽，群臣迎拜西掖門南，公下輿答拜，儐者請曰：「儀不拜。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the duke entered Luoyang; the ministers welcomed and bowed south of the western side gate; the duke descended from his carriage and returned the bow; the usher requested, saying: "By ritual one does not bow.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin he entered Luoyang; the ministers welcomed him south of the western side gate; he descended and returned their bows; the usher said, "By ritual you need not bow.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「吾人臣也。

translations.literal: " The duke said: "I am a subject.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I am a subject.

sentences.zh: 」遂答拜。

translations.literal: " He thereupon returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed in return.

sentences.zh: 至止車門下輿，左右曰：「舊乘輿入。

translations.literal: When he reached the Gate of Halting the Carriage he descended; those around him said: "By old custom one enters in the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the Gate of Halting the Carriage he descended; attendants said, "By old custom you enter in the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「吾被皇太后征，未知所為。

translations.literal: " The duke said: "I have been summoned by the empress dowager and do not yet know what is to be done.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I have been summoned by the empress dowager and do not yet know my role.

sentences.zh: 」遂步至太極東堂，見太后。

translations.literal: " He thereupon walked to the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate and saw the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: " He walked to the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate and met the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 其日，即皇帝位於太極前殿，百僚陪位者皆欣欣焉。

translations.literal: That same day he took the imperial throne in the front hall of the Supreme Ultimate; the hundred officials attending in place were all joyful.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he took the throne in the front hall of the Supreme Ultimate; the officials in attendance were all joyful.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 為齊王築宮於河內。

translations.literal: A palace was built for the Prince of Qi in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: A palace was built for the Prince of Qi in Henei.

sentences.zh: 漢姜維自鍬道進拔河間、臨洮。

translations.literal: Shu’s Jiang Wei advanced from Qiaodao and captured Hejian and Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei of Shu advanced from Qiaodao and captured Hejian and Lintao.

sentences.zh: 將軍徐質與戰，殺其蕩寇將軍張嶷，漢兵乃還。

translations.literal: General Xu Zhi fought him and killed his General Who Quells Bandits Zhang Ni; the Han troops then returned.
translations.idiomatic: General Xu Zhi fought him and killed his General Who Quells Bandits Zhang Ni; the Shu army then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，揚州刺史文欽，驍果絕人，曹爽以鄉里故愛之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Yangzhou Wen Qin was fierce and valiant beyond other men; Cao Shuang because of their shared native place favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wen Qin, Inspector of Yangzhou, was a warrior of exceptional ferocity; Cao Shuang favored him as a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 欽恃爽勢，多所陵傲。

translations.literal: Qin relied on Shuang’s power and in many matters was overbearing and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Qin relied on Shuang's power and bullied many men.

sentences.zh: 及爽誅，欽已內懼，又好增虜級以邀功賞，司馬師常抑之，由是怨望。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, Qin was already inwardly afraid; he also liked to inflate enemy head-counts to seek rewards; Sima Shi often curbed him—thereby he bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang was executed Qin grew fearful inwardly; he also inflated enemy kill counts to win rewards; Sima Shi often curbed him, and resentment grew.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍毌丘儉素與夏侯玄、李豐善，玄等死，儉亦不自安，乃以計厚待欽。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian had long been on good terms with Xiahou Xuan and Li Feng; when Xuan and the others died, Jian also was not at ease, and therefore by design treated Qin generously.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian had long been close to Xiahou Xuan and Li Feng; when they died Jian too felt insecure and deliberately treated Qin generously.

sentences.zh: 儉子治書侍御史甸謂儉曰：「大人居方岳重任，國家傾覆而晏然自守，將受四海之責矣！

translations.literal: Jian’s son Supervising Secretary Attendant Xun said to Jian: "Father, you hold the weighty responsibility of a frontier commander; the state is overturned yet you calmly hold yourself aloof—you will incur the blame of all within the seas!
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Xun, Supervising Secretary Attendant, told him, "Father, you hold a frontier commander's heavy responsibility; the state is in crisis yet you hold aloof—you will bear the blame of all under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」儉然之。

translations.literal: " Jian agreed that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公下正元二年（

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Duke of Shaoling, second year of Zhengyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Duke of Shaoling, second year of Zhengyuan (

sentences.zh: 乙亥，公元二五五年）

translations.literal: yihai, AD 255)
translations.idiomatic: the year yihai, AD 255)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，儉、欽矯太后詔，起兵於壽春，移檄州郡，以討司馬師。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Jian and Qin forged an empress dowager edict, raised troops at Shouchun, and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies to attack Sima Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin forged an edict in the Empress Dowager's name, raised an army at Shouchun, and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies denouncing Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 又表言：「相國懿忠正，有大勳於社稷，宜宥及後世，請廢師，以侯就第，以弟昭代之。

translations.literal: They also submitted a memorial stating: "The Chancellor Yi was loyal and upright and rendered great service to the state; his merit should extend to posterity. We request that Shi be deposed, that he retire to his marquisate, and that his younger brother Zhao replace him.
translations.idiomatic: They also submitted a memorial: "Chancellor Sima Yi was loyal and upright and rendered great service to the state; his merit should shield his descendants. We ask that Sima Shi be removed from office, retire to his marquisate as a noble, and be replaced by his younger brother Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 太尉孚忠孝小心，護軍望，忠公親事，皆宜親寵，授以要任。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Fu is filial, loyal, and careful; Protector of the Army Wang; Palace Attendant Zhong Yao—all should receive intimate favor and be entrusted with critical duties.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Sima Fu is dutiful, loyal, and careful; Protector of the Army Guo Wang; Palace Attendant Zhong Yao—all should be brought close, honored, and given posts of critical importance.

sentences.zh: 」望，孚之子也。

translations.literal: " Wang was Fu's son.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang was Sima Fu's son.

sentences.zh: 儉又遣使邀鎮南將軍諸葛誕，誕斬其使。

translations.literal: Jian again sent emissaries to invite General Who Guards the South Zhuge Dan; Dan beheaded the emissaries.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian sent envoys to win over General Who Guards the South Zhuge Dan, but Dan executed them.

sentences.zh: 儉、欽將五六萬眾渡淮，西至項；

translations.literal: Jian and Qin led fifty or sixty thousand men across the Huai, proceeding west to Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin crossed the Huai with fifty or sixty thousand troops and marched west to Xiang;

sentences.zh: 儉堅守，使欽在外為遊兵。

translations.literal: Jian held firm defense while sending Qin outside as a roving force.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian held the line while assigning Wen Qin to operate as mobile skirmishers outside.

sentences.zh: 司馬師問計於河南尹王肅，肅曰：「昔關羽虜于禁於漢濱，有北向爭天下之志，後孫權襲取其將士家屬，羽士眾一旦瓦解。

translations.literal: Sima Shi asked counsel of Intendant of Henan Wang Su, who said: "Formerly Guan Yu captured Yu Jin on the Han riverside and had the ambition to contend for the empire northward; later Sun Quan seized the families of his officers and soldiers, and Yu's forces collapsed in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi sought advice from Intendant of Henan Wang Su. Wang Su said, "When Guan Yu once captured Yu Jin on the Han River and turned north with ambitions to dominate the realm, Sun Quan raided and took the families of his troops—and Guan Yu's army collapsed overnight.

sentences.zh: 今淮南將士父母妻子皆在內州，但急往御衛，使不得前，必有關羽土崩之勢矣。

translations.literal: Now the officers and soldiers of Huainan all have parents, wives, and children in the interior provinces; if you hurry to guard and defend those places so the enemy cannot advance, there will surely be the same collapse as with Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Huainan troops' parents, wives, and children are all in the interior. If you rush to protect the homeland and block them from advancing north, you'll get the same chain-reaction collapse Guan Yu's army suffered.

sentences.zh: 」時師新割目瘤，創甚，或以為大將軍不宜自行，不如遣太尉孚拒之。

translations.literal: " At the time Shi had newly had an eye tumor cut away and his wound was severe; some thought the Grand General ought not go in person and that it would be better to send Grand Commandant Fu to resist.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi had just had an eye tumor removed; the wound was grave. Some argued the Grand General should not take the field in person and that Grand Commandant Sima Fu should be sent to hold the rebels instead.

sentences.zh: 唯王肅與尚書傅嘏、中書侍郎鐘會勸師自行，師疑未決。

translations.literal: Only Wang Su, together with Master of Writing Fu Gu and Secretariat Gentleman Zhong Hui, urged Shi to go in person; Shi hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Su, Master of Writing Fu Gu, and Secretariat Attendant Zhong Hui urged Sima Shi to lead the campaign himself; still, he wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 嘏曰：「淮、楚兵勁，而儉等負力遠鬥，其鋒未易當也。

translations.literal: Gu said: "The soldiers of Huai and Chu are strong, and Jian and the others are fighting far from home relying on their strength; their edge will not be easy to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gu said, "The Huai and Chu troops are formidable, and men like Guanqiu Jian are staking everything on a distant fight—their momentum won't be easy to stop.

sentences.zh: 若諸將戰有利鈍，大勢一失，則公事敗矣。

translations.literal: If the generals' battles have ups and downs and the overall momentum is once lost, then Your Excellency's enterprise will fail.
translations.idiomatic: If the field commanders win some engagements and lose others, one slip in the overall situation will ruin everything.

sentences.zh: 」師蹶然起曰：「我請輿疾而東。

translations.literal: " Shi suddenly rose and said: "I request to go east despite my illness, carried in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi leapt up and declared, "I'll go east by litter if I must.

sentences.zh: 」戊午，師率中外諸軍以討儉、欽，以弟昭兼中領軍，留鎮洛陽，召三方兵會於陳、許。

translations.literal: " On wu-wu, Shi led all the armies within and without to attack Jian and Qin; he had his younger brother Zhao additionally serve as Central Camp Commander to remain and guard Luoyang, and summoned troops from the three directions to assemble at Chen and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: " On wu-wu, Sima Shi marched with all imperial forces against Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin. He left his brother Sima Zhao as acting Central Camp Commander to hold Luoyang and called up armies from three directions to concentrate at Chen and Xu.

sentences.zh: 師問計於光祿勳鄭袤，袤曰：「毌丘儉好謀而不達事情，文欽勇而無算。

translations.literal: Shi asked counsel of Household Minister Zheng Mao, who said: "Guanqiu Jian likes plotting but does not grasp how things really stand; Wen Qin is brave but without calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi consulted Household Minister Zheng Mao, who said, "Guanqiu Jian loves scheming but doesn't understand the real situation; Wen Qin is brave but reckless.

sentences.zh: 今大軍出其不意，江、淮之卒，銳而不能固，宜深溝高壘以挫其氣，此亞夫之長策也。

translations.literal: Now if the great army strikes them unexpectedly, the troops of the Yangtze and Huai are sharp but cannot hold firm; you should dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts to break their momentum—this is the supreme stratagem of [Zhou] Yafu.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden strike by your main force will catch them off guard. Yangtze–Huai troops fight hard but won't hold. Dig deep trenches, raise high walls, and break their spirit—that's Zhou Yafu's sure method.

sentences.zh: 」師稱善。

translations.literal: " Shi praised this as good.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 師以荊州刺史王基為行監軍，假節，統許昌軍。

translations.literal: Shi appointed Inspector of Jing Wang Ji as acting overseer of the army, granted him the staff of authority, and put him in command of the Xuchang army.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi made Inspector of Jing Wang Ji acting army overseer with plenipotentiary staff, commanding the Xuchang forces.

sentences.zh: 基言於師曰：「淮南之逆，非吏民思亂也，儉等誑誘迫脅，畏目下之戮，是以尚屯聚耳。

translations.literal: Ji said to Shi: "The rebellion in Huainan is not because officials and people wished disorder; Jian and the others deceived, enticed, and coerced them, and they fear immediate execution—therefore they still mass together, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji told Sima Shi, "The Huainan revolt isn't popular unrest. Guanqiu Jian and his allies lied, enticed, and coerced people who now fear immediate punishment—that's why they're still gathered.

sentences.zh: 若大兵一臨，必土崩瓦解，儉、欽之首不終朝而致於軍門矣。

translations.literal: If the great army arrives once, they will surely collapse like a wall of earth; the heads of Jian and Qin will reach the camp gate before the morning is out.
translations.idiomatic: Once your main army appears, they'll crumble. Guanqiu Jian's and Wen Qin's heads will be at your gate before noon.

sentences.zh: 」師從之。

translations.literal: " Shi followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi agreed.

sentences.zh: 以基為前軍，既而復敕基停駐。

translations.literal: Ji was made vanguard; afterward an order came again instructing Ji to halt and stand fast.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji was placed at the head of the army, but soon Sima Shi ordered him to halt.

sentences.zh: 基以為：「儉等舉軍足以深入，而久不進者，是其詐偽已露，眾心疑沮也。

translations.literal: Ji believed: "Jian and the others raised an army sufficient to penetrate deep, yet for long they have not advanced—their deceit and pretense are already exposed and the hearts of the masses are wavering and discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji argued, "Guanqiu Jian raised an army strong enough to push deep inland, yet they've stalled for days. Their bluff is showing and morale is cracking.

sentences.zh: 今不張示威形以副民望，而停軍高壘，有似畏懦，非用兵之勢也。

translations.literal: Now if we do not display imposing might to satisfy popular expectation but instead halt the army behind high ramparts, it will seem like timidity—not the posture of employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: If we don't show decisive strength to meet public expectations and instead sit behind high walls, we'll look timid—that's no way to fight a war.

sentences.zh: 若儉、欽虜略民人以自益，又州郡兵家為賊所得者，更懷離心，儉等所迫脅者，自顧罪重，不敢復還，此為錯兵無用之地而成奸宄之源，吳寇因之，則淮南非國家之有，譙、沛、汝、豫危而不安，此計之大失也。

translations.literal: If Jian and Qin plunder and seize the people for their own benefit, and moreover those whose military households in the provinces and commanderies have fallen into the rebels' hands again harbor thoughts of separation, while those coerced by Jian and the others, considering their crimes grave, dare not return—this puts troops to waste in useless places and creates a source of villainy; if Wu's raiders take advantage, then Huainan will no longer belong to the state, and Qiao, Pei, Ru, and Yu will be endangered and unsettled—this would be a great failure of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: If Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin loot civilians for their own gain, and families of soldiers captured across the region turn against us, the coerced troops—knowing they'll face heavy punishment—won't dare come back. We'd be wasting armies in the wrong places and breeding new unrest. Wu could exploit the chaos, Huainan would slip from imperial control, and Qiao, Pei, Ru, and Yu would all be at risk. That would be a catastrophic mistake.

sentences.zh: 軍宜速進據南頓，南頓有大邸閣，計足軍人四十日糧。

translations.literal: The army ought quickly to advance and occupy Nandun; Nandun has a great depot, reckoned sufficient for the troops' forty days of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The army should push quickly to seize Nandun. Its great depot holds enough grain for forty days.

sentences.zh: 保堅城，因積穀，先人有奪人之心，此平賊之要也。

translations.literal: Hold a strong city and rely on accumulated grain; whoever is first gains the heart to seize from others—this is the key to pacifying the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Secure a strong city, stockpile grain, and seize the initiative—that's how you break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」基屢請，乃聽，進據水隱水。

translations.literal: " Ji repeatedly petitioned and was at last heeded; he advanced and occupied Shuiyin.
translations.idiomatic: " After repeated pleas from Wang Ji, Sima Shi relented, and the army advanced to occupy Shuiyin.

sentences.zh: 閏月，甲申，師次於水隱橋，儉將史招、李續相次來降。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jia-shen, Shi halted at Shuiyin Bridge; Jian's generals Shi Zhao and Li Xu came over to surrender one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jia-shen, Sima Shi camped at Shuiyin Bridge. Guanqiu Jian's officers Shi Zhao and Li Xu surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 王基復言於師曰：「兵聞拙速，未睹巧之久也。

translations.literal: Wang Ji again said to Shi: "In warfare one has heard of clumsy speed, but never of skillful delay.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji again told Sima Shi, "In war, clumsy haste is praised; prolonged cleverness is never seen.

sentences.zh: 方今外有強寇，內有叛臣，若不時決，則事之深淺未可測也。

translations.literal: At present there are strong enemies abroad and rebel ministers within; if the issue is not decided in time, whether matters end shallow or deep cannot be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Right now there are powerful enemies abroad and rebel ministers within. If we don't settle this quickly, no one can say how far the damage will spread.

sentences.zh: 議者多言將軍持重。

translations.literal: Those in counsel say much that the General should act with weight and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Many in council say the General should act with deliberation.

sentences.zh: 將軍持重，是也；

translations.literal: That the General should be deliberate is right;
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation is right;

sentences.zh: 停軍不進，非也。

translations.literal: to halt the army and not advance is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: but halting the army and refusing to advance is wrong.

sentences.zh: 持重，非不得之謂也，進而不可犯耳。

translations.literal: "Deliberation" does not mean doing nothing—it means advancing in a way no one can withstand.
translations.idiomatic: "Deliberation" doesn't mean standing still—it means advancing in a way no one can withstand.

sentences.zh: 今保壁壘以積實資虜而遠運軍糧，甚非計也。

translations.literal: Now to hold behind ramparts, accumulating stores that enrich the enemy while transporting army grain from afar—this is a very poor plan.
translations.idiomatic: Sitting behind walls while stockpiles feed the enemy and grain must be hauled from afar is a terrible plan.

sentences.zh: 」師猶未許。

translations.literal: " Shi still did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi still would not agree.

sentences.zh: 基曰：「將在軍，君令有所不受。

translations.literal: Ji said: "The general in the field may disregard orders from his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said, "A general in the field may disregard his lord's orders.

sentences.zh: 彼得則利，我得亦利，是謂爭地，南頓是也。

translations.literal: If they gain it they profit, if we gain it we also profit—this is called contended ground; Nandun is such a place.
translations.idiomatic: If they take it, they gain; if we take it, we gain. That is contended ground—and Nandun is exactly that.

sentences.zh: 」遂輒進據南頓，儉等從項亦欲往爭，發十餘里，聞基先到，乃復還保項。

translations.literal: " He then advanced on his own authority to occupy Nandun. Jian and the others, also wishing to contest it from Xiang, set out for more than ten li but, learning Ji had arrived first, turned back to hold Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then advanced on his own authority and seized Nandun. Guanqiu Jian and his allies, marching from Xiang to contest the same ground, had gone little more than ten li when they learned Wang Ji had arrived first; they turned back and held Xiang.

sentences.zh: 癸未，征西將軍郭淮卒，以雍州刺史陳泰代之。

translations.literal: On gui-wei, General Who Conquers the West Guo Huai died; Inspector of Yong Chen Tai was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: On gui-wei, General Who Conquers the West Guo Huai died, and Inspector of Yong Chen Tai was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 吳丞相峻率驃騎將軍呂據、左將軍會稽留贊襲壽春，司馬師命諸軍皆深壁高壘，以待東軍之集。

translations.literal: Wu Chancellor Sun Jun led Flying Cavalry General Lü Ju and General of the Left Liu Zan of Kuaiji in a raid on Shouchun. Sima Shi ordered all armies to dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts, waiting for the eastern troops to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chancellor Sun Jun led Flying Cavalry General Lü Ju and General of the Left Liu Zan of Kuaiji in a raid on Shouchun. Sima Shi ordered every army to dig deep trenches and raise high walls while waiting for the eastern forces to concentrate.

sentences.zh: 諸將請進軍攻項，師曰：「諸軍得其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: The generals requested to advance and attack Xiang. Shi said: "You generals have grasped one point but do not know the second.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked to advance and attack Xiang. Sima Shi said, "You have grasped one point but not the second.

sentences.zh: 淮南將士本無反志，儉、欽說誘與之舉事，謂遠近必應；

translations.literal: The Huainan officers and soldiers originally had no intent to rebel; Jian and Qin persuaded and enticed them into raising the affair, saying those near and far would surely respond;
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan troops never wanted rebellion in the first place. Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin talked them into rising, promising that allies near and far would answer;

sentences.zh: 而事起之日，淮北不從，史招、李繼前後瓦解，內乖外叛，自知必敗。

translations.literal: yet when the affair began, Huai-bei did not follow; Shi Zhao and Li Ji successively collapsed; within they were at odds and without they were betrayed—they knew themselves certain to fail.
translations.idiomatic: yet when the revolt began, Huai-bei did not join them. Shi Zhao and Li Ji defected one after another. Discord spread within and loyalty failed without—they knew they were doomed.

sentences.zh: 困獸思鬥，速戰更合其志。

translations.literal: A cornered beast thinks only of fighting; a quick battle would suit their purpose all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered beasts fight hardest—a quick battle is exactly what they want.

sentences.zh: 雖雲必克，傷人亦多。

translations.literal: Even if victory is assured, casualties would also be many.
translations.idiomatic: We might win, but at heavy cost.

sentences.zh: 且儉等欺誑將士，詭變萬端，小與持久，詐情自露，此不戰而克之術也。

translations.literal: Moreover Jian and the others deceive the officers and soldiers with countless shifts and tricks; contest them a little while longer and their falsehoods will expose themselves—this is the method of conquering without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin have deceived their troops with endless ruses. Hold them a little longer and their lies will unravel—that is how you win without fighting.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣諸葛誕督豫州諸軍，自安風向壽春；

translations.literal: " He then sent Zhuge Dan to oversee the armies of Yu Province, marching from Anfeng toward Shouchun;
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Zhuge Dan to command the armies of Yu Province, marching from Anfeng toward Shouchun;

sentences.zh: 征東將軍胡遵督青、徐諸軍出譙、宋之間，絕其歸路；

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the East Hu Zun to oversee the armies of Qing and Xu, issuing from between Qiao and Song to cut off their route of retreat;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the East Hu Zun to command the armies of Qing and Xu, issuing from between Qiao and Song to cut off their retreat;

sentences.zh: 師屯汝陽。

translations.literal: Shi encamped at Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi encamped at Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉、文欽進不得鬥，退恐壽春見襲，計窮不知所為。

translations.literal: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin could not advance to fight, and if they retreated feared Shouchun would be attacked; their plans exhausted, they knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin could neither advance to fight nor retreat without fearing an attack on Shouchun. Their options exhausted, they did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 淮南將士家皆在北，眾心沮散，降者相屬，惟淮南新附農民為之用。

translations.literal: The families of Huainan officers and soldiers were all in the north; hearts were discouraged and scattered, and those surrendering followed one after another—only newly attached peasants of Huainan still served them.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan troops' families were all in the north. Morale collapsed and surrenders came in waves—only newly settled Huainan peasants still fought for them.

sentences.zh: 儉之初起，遣健步繼書至兗州，兗州刺史鄧艾斬之，將兵萬餘人，兼道前進，先趨樂嘉城，作浮橋以待師。

translations.literal: When Jian first rose, he sent runners in relays with letters to Yan Province; Inspector of Yan Deng Ai beheaded them, led more than ten thousand troops by forced marches, and pressed ahead first toward Lecheng, building a pontoon bridge to await Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian first rose, he sent runners in relays with messages to Yan Province. Inspector of Yan Deng Ai executed them, then led more than ten thousand men by forced marches to Lecheng, where he built a pontoon bridge to await Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 儉使文欽將兵襲之。

translations.literal: Jian sent Wen Qin at the head of troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian sent Wen Qin with troops to attack them.

sentences.zh: 師自汝陽潛兵就艾於樂嘉，欽猝見大軍，驚愕未知所為。

translations.literal: Shi secretly moved troops from Ruyang to join Ai at Lecheng. Qin suddenly saw the great army and was astonished, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi secretly marched from Ruyang to join Deng Ai at Lecheng. Wen Qin was stunned to see the main army appear and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 欽子鴦，年十八，勇力絕人，謂欽曰：「及其未定，擊之，可破也。

translations.literal: Qin's son Yang, eighteen years old, with courage and strength surpassing others, said to Qin: "While they are not yet settled, strike them—we can break them.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin's son Wen Yang, eighteen years old and possessed of extraordinary courage and strength, said to his father, "Strike before they settle—we can break them.

sentences.zh: 」於是分為二隊，夜夾攻軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they divided into two contingents and by night attacked the army from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: " They split into two columns and attacked the imperial army from both sides that night.

sentences.zh: 鴦率壯士先至鼓噪，軍中震擾。

translations.literal: Yang led stalwart warriors to arrive first with drumming and shouting; the army was shaken and thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang led the picked warriors in first, drumming and shouting. The imperial camp was thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 師驚駭。

translations.literal: Shi was alarmed and frightened.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi was terrified.

sentences.zh: 所病目突出，恐眾知之，嚙被皆破。

translations.literal: The eye that had been afflicted bulged out; fearing the troops would know, he bit through his bedding completely.
translations.idiomatic: The diseased eye bulged from its socket. Fearing the troops would see, he bit through his bedding to stifle any cry.

sentences.zh: 欽失期不應，會明，鴦見兵盛，乃引還。

translations.literal: Qin failed to arrive on time and did not respond; when dawn came, Yang saw the enemy ranks were strong and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin failed to arrive on schedule. At dawn Wen Yang saw how strong the imperial forces were and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 師謂諸將曰：「賊走矣，可追之！

translations.literal: Shi told the generals: "The rebels have fled—we can pursue them!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi told his generals, "The rebels are fleeing—we can pursue them!

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「欽父子驍猛，未有所屈，何苦而走？

translations.literal: " The generals said: "The Qin father and son are fierce and bold—they have not been broken in any way; why would they flee for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: " The generals said, "The Wen father and son are ferocious—they haven't been beaten yet. Why would they run for no reason?

sentences.zh: 」師曰：「夫一鼓作氣，再而衰。

translations.literal: " Shi said: "At the first drum spirits are roused; at the second they fade.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi said, "At the first drum, spirits rise; at the second, they fade.

sentences.zh: 鴦鼓噪失應，其勢已屈，不走何待！

translations.literal: Yang drummed and shouted but got no response—their momentum is already spent. Why wouldn't they flee?
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang drummed and shouted but got no answer—their momentum is spent. Of course they ran!

sentences.zh: 」欽將引而東，鴦曰：「不先折其勢，不得也。

translations.literal: " Qin was about to lead the army east when Yang said: "Unless we first break their momentum, we cannot get away.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen Qin was about to march east when Wen Yang said, "Unless we break their momentum first, we won't get away.

sentences.zh: 」乃與驍騎十餘摧鋒陷陳，所向皆披靡，遂引去。

translations.literal: " Then with more than ten picked horsemen he smashed the van and broke the battle line; wherever he went all were routed, and he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took a dozen picked horsemen, smashed the van, broke the line, routed everything in his path, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 師使左長史司馬班率驍將八千翼而追之，鴦以匹馬入數千騎中，輒殺傷百餘人，乃出，如此者六七，追騎莫敢逼。

translations.literal: Shi sent Left Chief Clerk Sima Ban at the head of eight thousand crack officers to pursue from the flank. Yang, on a single horse, entered among several thousand cavalrymen and each time killed or wounded more than a hundred before coming out—this he did six or seven times, and the pursuers did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi sent Left Chief Clerk Sima Ban with eight thousand crack officers in flanking pursuit. Wen Yang, alone on horseback, plunged into thousands of enemy cavalry, killing or wounding more than a hundred each time before breaking out—six or seven times in all—and the pursuers did not dare close on him.

sentences.zh: 殿中人尹大目小為曹氏家奴，常在天子左右，師將與俱行，大目知師一目已出，啟云：「文欽本是明公腹心，但為人所誤耳；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yin Damu had once been a household slave of the Cao clan and was often at the Son of Heaven's side. Shi was about to go with him. Damu knew one of Shi's eyes had bulged out and submitted: "Wen Qin was originally Your Excellency's trusted confidant—he was merely led astray by others;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yin Damu had once been a household slave of the Cao clan and was often at the emperor's side. Sima Shi was about to take him along. Damu knew one of Shi's eyes had bulged out and petitioned: "Wen Qin was once Your Excellency's trusted confidant—others merely misled him;

sentences.zh: 又天子鄉里，素與大目相信，乞為公追解語之，令還與公復好。

translations.literal: moreover, as a fellow townsman of the imperial clan, he has long trusted me. I beg to ride after him and mediate, that he may return and renew friendship with Your Excellency.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, as a fellow townsman of the imperial house, he has long trusted me. I beg leave to ride after him and mediate, so he may return and renew his bond with Your Excellency.

sentences.zh: 」師許之。

translations.literal: " Shi consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Shi agreed.

sentences.zh: 大目單身乘大馬，被鎧冑，追欽，遙相與語。

translations.literal: Damu alone mounted a great horse, donned armor, pursued Qin, and spoke with him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Damu rode out alone on a great horse, armored, pursued Wen Qin, and spoke with him from a distance.

sentences.zh: 大目心實欲為曹氏，謬言：「君侯何苦不可復忍數日中也！

translations.literal: In his heart Damu truly wished to serve the house of Cao and spoke falsely: "My lord, why need you suffer? In a few days more you cannot bear it!
translations.idiomatic: In his heart Yin Damu truly wished to serve the house of Cao and spoke deceptively: "My lord, why endure such hardship? In a few days you won't be able to bear it!

sentences.zh: 」欲使欽解其旨。

translations.literal: " He meant for Qin to grasp his intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant for Wen Qin to grasp his meaning.

sentences.zh: 欽殊不悟，乃更厲聲罵大目曰：「汝先帝家人，不念報恩，反與司馬師作逆，不顧上天，天不祐汝！

translations.literal: Qin did not understand at all; instead he shouted and reviled Damu all the louder: "You are a kinsman of the former Emperor—you do not think of repaying gratitude but instead join Sima Shi in rebellion, heedless of Heaven; Heaven will not protect you!
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin did not understand at all. Instead he shouted and reviled Yin Damu all the louder: "You are kin to the late Emperor—you forget your debt of gratitude and join Sima Shi in rebellion, heedless of Heaven. Heaven will not protect you!

sentences.zh: 」張弓傅矢欲射大目。

translations.literal: " He drew his bow, nocked an arrow, and tried to shoot Damu.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his bow, nocked an arrow, and tried to shoot Yin Damu.

sentences.zh: 大目涕泣曰：「世事敗矣，善自努力！

translations.literal: Damu wept and said: "The cause is lost—fare well and do your best!
translations.idiomatic: Yin Damu wept and said, "The cause is lost—fare well and do your best!

sentences.zh: 是日，毌丘儉聞欽退，恐懼，夜走，眾遂大潰。

translations.literal: That day, when Guanqiu Jian heard Qin had withdrawn, he was afraid and fled by night; the army then routed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: That day, when Guanqiu Jian learned Wen Qin had withdrawn, he panicked and fled by night. The army then collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 欽還至項，以孤軍無繼，不能自立，欲還壽春；

translations.literal: Qin returned to Xiang; as an isolated army without reinforcement he could not stand alone and wished to return to Shouchun;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin returned to Xiang. As an isolated force without reinforcements, he could not hold his ground and wanted to return to Shouchun;

sentences.zh: 壽春已潰，遂奔吳。

translations.literal: Shouchun had already collapsed, so he fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun had already fallen, so he fled to Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳孫峻至東興，聞儉等敗，壬寅，進至橐皋，文欽父子詣軍降。

translations.literal: Sun Jun of Wu reached Dongxing; hearing Jian and the others were defeated, on ren-yin he advanced to Tuogao, and Wen Qin and his son came to the army to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun of Wu reached Dongxing. Hearing that Guanqiu Jian and his allies had been defeated, on ren-yin he advanced to Tuogao, where Wen Qin and his son came to the army and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉走，比至慎縣，左右人兵稍棄儉去，儉藏水邊草中。

translations.literal: Guanqiu Jian fled; by the time he reached Shen county, the troops around him gradually abandoned him and left. Jian hid in the grass beside the water.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian fled. By the time he reached Shen county, his followers had gradually abandoned him. He hid in the grass beside the water.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，安風津民張屬就殺儉，傳首京師，封屬為侯。

translations.literal: On jia-chen, Zhang Shu of Anfeng Ford went and killed Jian, sent the head to the capital, and Shu was enfeoffed as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-chen, Zhang Shu of Anfeng Ford tracked down and killed Guanqiu Jian, sent the head to the capital, and was enfeoffed as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕至壽春，壽春城中十餘萬口，懼誅，或流迸山澤，或散走入吳。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Dan reached Shouchun, the more than a hundred thousand people in the city, fearing execution, either scattered into mountains and marshes or dispersed and fled into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan reached Shouchun, the city's population of more than a hundred thousand, fearing execution, either fled into the hills and marshes or scattered into Wu territory.

sentences.zh: 詔以誕為鎮東大將軍、儀同三司，都督揚州諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Dan General Who Guards the East with Protocol Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, overseeing all military affairs of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhuge Dan General Who Guards the East with Protocol Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, with overall command of military affairs in Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 夷毌丘儉三族。

translations.literal: The three clans of Guanqiu Jian were exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: The three clans of Guanqiu Jian were exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 儉黨七百餘人繫獄，侍御史杜友治之，惟誅首事者十餘人，餘皆奏免之。

translations.literal: More than seven hundred of Jian's faction were imprisoned; Attendant Censor Du You handled the case, executing only the dozen or so who had led the affair and memorializing to pardon the rest.
translations.idiomatic: More than seven hundred of Guanqiu Jian's followers were imprisoned. Attendant Censor Du You handled the case, executing only the dozen or so ringleaders and memorializing to pardon the rest.

sentences.zh: 儉孫女適劉氏，當死，以孕系廷尉。

translations.literal: Jian's granddaughter, married to the Liu family, was liable to death but, being pregnant, was held at the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian's granddaughter, married into the Liu family, was sentenced to death but, being pregnant, was held at the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 司隸主簿程鹹議曰：「女適人者，若已產育，則成他家之母，於防則不足懲奸亂之源，於情則傷孝子之恩。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Metropolitan Commandery Cheng Xian submitted a proposal: "When a woman has married out, if she has already borne children, she becomes a mother in another house; as a deterrent this is insufficient to punish the source of treachery and disorder, and in human feeling it wounds the grace owed to filial sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Metropolitan Commandery Cheng Xian submitted a proposal: "When a woman has married out and already borne children, she becomes a mother in another household. Executing her neither deters the roots of treason nor honors the claims of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 男不遇罪於他族，而女獨嬰戮於二門，非所以哀矜女弱、均法制之大分也。

translations.literal: A man does not meet punishment in another clan, yet a woman alone suffers execution touching two families—this is not the way to show pity for the weakness of women or to balance the great divisions of law.
translations.idiomatic: A man is not punished through another clan, yet a woman alone may be executed and harm two families—this is neither merciful toward women nor consistent with the great divisions of law.

sentences.zh: 臣以為在室之女，可從父母之刑；

translations.literal: Your subject believes that an unmarried daughter may follow her parents' punishment;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that an unmarried daughter may share her parents' punishment;

sentences.zh: 既醮之婦，使從夫家之戮。

translations.literal: a woman already wedded should follow her husband's family's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: but a woman already wedded should follow her husband's family's punishment.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之，仍著於律令。

translations.literal: " The court followed this and incorporated it into the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: " The court accepted the proposal and incorporated it into the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 舞陽忠武侯司馬師疾篤，還許昌，留中郎將參軍事賈充監諸軍事。

translations.literal: Sima Shi, Loyal and Martial Marquis of Wuyang, was gravely ill; he returned to Xuchang and left Gentleman of the Palace Jia Chong to oversee military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi, Loyal and Martial Marquis of Wuyang, fell gravely ill. He returned to Xuchang and left Gentleman of the Palace Jia Chong to oversee military affairs.

sentences.zh: 充，逵之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was the son of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong was the son of Jia Kui.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍昭自洛陽往省師，師令昭總統諸軍。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Zhao came from Luoyang to visit Shi; Shi ordered Zhao to take overall command of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Sima Zhao came from Luoyang to visit his brother. Sima Shi ordered Sima Zhao to take overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，師卒於許昌。

translations.literal: On xin-hai, Shi died at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On xin-hai, Sima Shi died at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎鐘會從師典知密事，中詔敕尚書傅嘏，以東南新定，權留衛將軍昭屯許昌為內外之援，令嘏率諸軍還。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhong Hui accompanied the army and managed confidential affairs; an imperial order was issued to Master of Writing Fu Gu: since the southeast had newly been pacified, Guard General Zhao was provisionally left stationed at Xuchang as support within and without, and Gu was ordered to lead all the armies back.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhong Hui had accompanied the army and managed confidential affairs. An imperial order reached Master of Writing Fu Gu: with the southeast newly pacified, Guard General Sima Zhao was to remain at Xuchang as a reserve for forces at home and abroad, while Gu led the main armies back.

sentences.zh: 會與嘏謀，使嘏表上，輒與昭俱發，還到洛水南屯住。

translations.literal: Hui plotted with Gu, had Gu submit a memorial, then set out together with Zhao, returned and encamped south of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Gu conspired: Gu would submit the memorial, then both would set out with Zhao and encamp south of the Luo River on the return march.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，詔以司馬昭為大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on ding-si, an edict appointed Sima Zhao Grand General and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on ding-si, an edict made Sima Zhao Grand General and put him in charge of recording the affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 會由是常有自矜之色，嘏戒之曰：「子志大其量，而勳業難為也，可不慎哉！

translations.literal: From this Hui often wore a self-satisfied look; Gu admonished him, saying: "Your ambitions exceed your capacity, and such achievements are hard to accomplish—should you not be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: From then on Hui often wore a self-satisfied air. Fu Gu warned him: "Your ambitions outrun your measure, and such deeds are hard to bring off—take care!"

sentences.zh: 吳孫峻聞諸葛誕已據壽春，乃引兵還。

translations.literal: In Wu, Sun Jun heard that Zhuge Dan had already seized Shouchun, and thereupon withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Sun Jun heard that Zhuge Dan had already taken Shouchun and withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 以文欽為都護、鎮北大將軍、幽州牧。

translations.literal: Wen Qin was appointed Chief Controller, Grand General Who Guards the North, and Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin was made Chief Controller, Grand General Who Guards the North, and Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，立皇后卞氏，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, Empress Bian was installed and a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Lady Bian was enthroned as empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 後，武宣皇后弟秉之曾孫女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the great-great-granddaughter of Bin, younger brother of Empress Wu-Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The new empress was a great-great-granddaughter of Bin, younger brother of Empress Wu-Xuan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳將軍孫儀、張怡、林恂謀殺孫峻，不克，死者數十人。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wu generals Sun Yi, Zhang Yi, and Lin Xun plotted to kill Sun Jun but failed; several dozen men died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Wu generals Sun Yi, Zhang Yi, and Lin Xun plotted to assassinate Sun Jun. The attempt failed, and several dozen men were killed.

sentences.zh: 全公主譖朱公主於峻，曰「與儀同謀」。

translations.literal: Princess Quan slandered Princess Zhu to Jun, saying "she had plotted together with Sun Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Quan denounced Princess Zhu to Sun Jun, claiming she had conspired with Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 峻遂殺朱公主。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon killed Princess Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun then had Princess Zhu executed.

sentences.zh: 峻使衛尉馮朝城廣陵，功費甚眾，舉朝莫敢言，唯滕胤諫止之，峻不從，功卒不成。

translations.literal: Jun had Minister of the Guard Feng Chao fortify Guangling; the labor and expense were enormous. The whole court dared not speak—only Teng Yin remonstrated and tried to stop it. Jun would not listen, and in the end the work was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun ordered Minister of the Guard Feng Chao to fortify Guangling. The project consumed vast labor and expense, and no one in court dared object—only Teng Yin remonstrated and tried to halt it. Jun refused to listen, and the work was never finished.

sentences.zh: 漢姜維復議出軍，征西大將軍張翼廷爭，以為：「國小民勞，不宜黷武。

translations.literal: In Han, Jiang Wei again proposed sending out the army; Campaign-West Grand General Zhang Yi contested it in court, arguing: "The state is small and the people are weary—it is not fitting to abuse military action."
translations.idiomatic: In Shu-Han, Jiang Wei again urged a campaign. Campaign-West Grand General Zhang Yi disputed him in open court, arguing: "The state is small and the people are exhausted—we should not wear them out with repeated warfare."

sentences.zh: 」維不聽，率車騎將軍夏侯霸及翼同進。

translations.literal: " Wei would not listen and led General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba and Zhang Yi forward together.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei would not listen. He led General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba and Zhang Yi forward together.

sentences.zh: 八月，維將數萬人至枹罕，趨狄道。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wei led several tens of thousands of men to Fuhan and hurried toward Didao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Jiang Wei led tens of thousands of men to Fuhan and pressed toward Didao.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍陳泰敕雍州刺史王經進屯狄道，須泰軍到，東西合勢乃進。

translations.literal: Campaign-West General Chen Tai ordered Yong Province Inspector Wang Jing to advance and encamp at Didao, and that only when Tai's army arrived should east and west combine their strength and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign-West General Chen Tai ordered Yong Province Inspector Wang Jing to advance and hold Didao, and not to move until Tai's own army arrived and their forces could unite east and west.

sentences.zh: 泰軍陳倉，經所統諸軍於故關與漢人戰不利，經輒渡洮水。

translations.literal: Tai's army was at Chencang; the forces under Wang Jing fought the Han at Gu Pass with poor results, and Jing immediately crossed the Tao River.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai's army was at Chencang. The troops under Wang Jing fought the Han forces at Gu Pass with poor results, and Jing at once crossed the Tao River.

sentences.zh: 泰以經不堅據狄道，必有他變，率諸軍以繼之。

translations.literal: Tai thought that since Jing had not firmly held Didao, there must be some other change of plan, and led all the armies to follow after him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai judged that Jing's failure to hold Didao firmly meant something had gone wrong, and led all his forces after him.

sentences.zh: 經已與維戰於洮西，大敗，以萬餘人還保狄道城，餘皆奔散，死者萬計。

translations.literal: Jing had already fought Wei west of the Tao and suffered a great defeat; he returned with more than ten thousand men to defend Didao city, while the rest scattered in flight—the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had already fought Jiang Wei west of the Tao and been routed. He returned with a little more than ten thousand men to hold Didao city while the rest fled in every direction; the dead were counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 張翼謂維曰：「可以止矣，不宜復進，進或毀此大功，為蛇畫足。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi said to Wei: "You can stop now. You should not advance further—advancing might ruin this great achievement, like drawing legs on a snake."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi told Jiang Wei: "You can stop here. You should not press on—going farther may spoil this great victory, like adding feet to a snake."

sentences.zh: 」維大怒，遂進圍狄道。

translations.literal: " Wei flew into a rage and pressed on to besiege Didao.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Wei flew into a rage and pressed on to besiege Didao.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔長水校尉鄧艾行安西將軍，與陳泰並力拒維；

translations.literal: On xin-wei, an edict ordered Colonel of the Changshui Deng Ai to act as Pacifier of the West and join Chen Tai in resisting Wei with combined strength;
translations.idiomatic: On xin-wei, an edict ordered Colonel of the Changshui Deng Ai to serve as acting Pacifier of the West and join Chen Tai in resisting Jiang Wei with all their strength;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，復以太尉孚為後繼。

translations.literal: On wu-chen, Grand Commandant Fu was again appointed as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-chen, Grand Commandant Sima Fu was again assigned as rear support.

sentences.zh: 泰進軍隴西，諸將皆曰：「王經新敗，賊眾大盛，將軍以烏合之卒，繼敗軍之後，當乘勝之鋒，殆必不可。

translations.literal: Tai advanced the army into Longxi. All the generals said: "Wang Jing has just been defeated, and the bandit forces are at their height. The General leads a hastily assembled band following a defeated army, to meet the edge of their victorious momentum—surely it cannot possibly succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai marched into Longxi. His generals all said: "Wang Jing has just been beaten, and the enemy is at full strength. You would lead a hastily gathered force in the wake of a routed army straight into the point of their victory—surely that cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『蝮蛇螫手，壯士解腕。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'When a viper bites the hand, the bold man cuts off his wrist.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "When a viper bites the hand, the resolute man severs his wrist."

sentences.zh: 』《孫子》曰：『兵有所不擊，地有所不守。

translations.literal: Sunzi says: 'There are times not to strike with the army, and places not to hold.'
translations.idiomatic: Sunzi says: "There are enemies one does not attack and ground one does not defend."

sentences.zh: 』蓋小有所失而大有所全故也。

translations.literal: This is because one accepts a small loss to preserve the whole.
translations.idiomatic: That is because one accepts a small loss in order to preserve the whole.

sentences.zh: 不如據險自保，觀釁待敝，然後進救，此計之得者也。

translations.literal: Better to hold strong positions and protect yourself, watch for openings and wait for them to tire, then advance to the rescue—this is the plan that succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the defensible ground, watch for an opening and wait until they tire, then move to relieve the city—that is the sound plan.

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「姜維提輕兵深入，正欲與我爭鋒原野，求一戰之利。

translations.literal: " Tai said: "Jiang Wei leads light troops deep in—he precisely wants to contest us in the open field and win the advantage of a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Tai replied: "Jiang Wei has led light troops deep into our territory because he wants to meet us in the open and win one decisive battle."

sentences.zh: 王經當高壁深壘，挫其銳氣，今乃與戰，使賊得計。

translations.literal: Wang Jing should have built high walls and deep ramparts to blunt their sharp spirit; instead he joined battle and let the bandits have their way.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing should have raised high walls and deep ramparts to break their momentum. Instead he gave battle and let the enemy have his way.

sentences.zh: 經既破走，維若以戰克之威，進兵東向，據櫟陽積穀之實，放兵收降，招納羌、胡，東爭關、隴，傳檄四郡，此我之所惡也。

translations.literal: Now that Jing is broken and fled, if Wei uses the prestige of his victory to advance eastward, seize the grain stores of Liyang, release his soldiers to accept surrenders, win over the Qiang and Hu, contest Guan and Long to the east, and spread proclamations through the four commanderies—this is what we most dread.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jing is broken and in flight, if Jiang Wei uses the prestige of victory to march east, seize the grain stored at Liyang, send his troops out to accept surrenders, win over the Qiang and Hu, contest Guan and Long, and issue proclamations across the four commanderies—that is what we most dread.

sentences.zh: 而乃以乘勝之兵，挫峻城之下，銳氣之卒，屈力致命，攻守勢殊，客主不同。

translations.literal: And yet he uses his victorious army to batter against a steep-walled city; troops at the height of their fighting spirit exhaust their strength in a death struggle—the conditions of attack and defense differ, and guest and host are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yet instead he uses his victorious army to batter a fortified city, forcing troops at the peak of their fighting spirit to spend their strength in a grim siege. The conditions of attack and defense differ, and the besieger and the besieged are not equals.

sentences.zh: 兵書曰：『修櫓轒轀，三月乃成，拒堙三月而後已。

translations.literal: The military texts say: 'Building siege towers and battering rams takes three months to complete; filling in moats takes three months before it ends.'
translations.idiomatic: The military texts say: "Building siege towers and battering rams takes three months; filling in moats takes three months more."

sentences.zh: 』誠非輕軍遠入之利也。

translations.literal: This is truly no advantage for lightly armed troops operating far from home.
translations.idiomatic: That is no advantage for a lightly equipped army operating far from home.

sentences.zh: 今維孤軍遠僑，糧谷不繼，是我速進破賊之時，所謂疾雷不及掩耳，自然之勢也。

translations.literal: Now Wei is a lone army far from support, with grain and provisions cut off—this is the moment for us to advance swiftly and break the bandits, what is called thunder so fast one cannot cover one's ears: the natural course of events.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jiang Wei is isolated far from home with his grain cut off. This is the moment for us to strike quickly and break the enemy—the thunder that outruns the hand clapped over the ears, the natural turn of events.

sentences.zh: 洮水帶其表，維等在其內，今乘高據勢，臨其項領，不戰必走。

translations.literal: The Tao River wraps around their front; Wei and his men are within it. If we now take the heights and hold the advantage, pressing on their necks, they will flee without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The Tao River lies across their front and Jiang Wei is penned within it. If we seize the high ground and press on their necks, they will flee without a fight.

sentences.zh: 寇不可縱，圍不可久，君等何言如是！

translations.literal: Bandits must not be indulged; a siege must not be prolonged—how can you speak like this!
translations.idiomatic: Bandits must not be indulged, and a siege must not be drawn out—how can you counsel otherwise!

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍度高城嶺，潛行，夜至狄道東南高山上，多舉烽火，鳴鼓角。

translations.literal: " He thereupon advanced the army over Gaocheng Ridge by hidden march, arriving by night at the high mountains southeast of Didao, where many beacon fires were raised and drums and horns sounded.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched over Gaocheng Ridge by concealed routes and by night reached the heights southeast of Didao, where he lit many beacon fires and sounded drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 狄道城中將士見救至，皆憤踴。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers in Didao city, seeing rescue arrive, all leaped up with renewed fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When the officers and soldiers in Didao saw relief arrive, they leaped up with renewed fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 維不意救兵卒至，緣山急來攻之，泰與交戰，維退。

translations.literal: Wei had not expected relief forces to arrive so suddenly; he hurried along the mountains to attack them. Tai joined battle with him and Wei withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei had not expected relief to arrive so suddenly. He hurried along the mountains to attack, but Chen Tai met him in battle and Wei withdrew.

sentences.zh: 泰引兵揚言欲向其還路，維懼，九月，甲辰，維遁走，城中將士乃得出。

translations.literal: Tai led his troops, proclaiming his intent to strike their line of retreat. Wei grew fearful; in the ninth month, on jia-chen, Wei fled, and only then could the officers and soldiers in the city get out.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai marched his troops while proclaiming that he would cut off the enemy's retreat. Jiang Wei grew afraid; in the ninth month, on jia-chen, he fled, and only then could the city's defenders come out.

sentences.zh: 王經歎曰：「糧不至旬，向非救兵速至，舉城屠裂，覆喪一州矣！

translations.literal: Wang Jing sighed and said: "Our grain would not have lasted ten days. Had relief not arrived so quickly, the whole city would have been slaughtered and one whole province lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing sighed and said: "Our grain would not have lasted ten days. Had relief not come so quickly, the whole city would have been slaughtered and an entire province lost!"

sentences.zh: 」泰慰勞將士，前後遣還，更差軍守，並治城壘，還屯上邽。

translations.literal: " Tai comforted and rewarded the officers and soldiers, sent them back in stages, reassigned garrisons, repaired the city fortifications together, and returned to encamp at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Tai comforted and rewarded the troops, sent them back in stages, reassigned garrisons, repaired the fortifications, and returned to encamp at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 泰每以一方有事，輒以虛聲擾動天下，故希簡上事，驛書不過六百里。

translations.literal: Tai, because any affair in one region would stir the whole empire with inflated reports, therefore preferred to keep his memorials brief; his courier dispatches never exceeded six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai knew that trouble in one region often set the whole empire astir with exaggerated reports, so he kept his memorials brief and his courier dispatches never traveled more than six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 大將軍昭曰：「陳征西沉勇能斷，荷方伯之重，救將陷之城，而不求益兵，又希簡上事，必能辦賊故也。

translations.literal: Grand General Zhao said: "Campaign-West Chen is deep, brave, and decisive; bearing the weight of a regional command, he rescued a city about to fall yet did not ask for reinforcements, and also kept his reports brief—he must have been confident he could handle the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Zhao said: "Campaign-West Chen is steady, brave, and decisive. Bearing the weight of a frontier command, he rescued a city on the brink of fall without asking for reinforcements and kept his reports brief—he must have known he could handle the enemy."

sentences.zh: 都督大將不當爾邪！

translations.literal: Should not a commanding grand general be just such a man!
translations.idiomatic: Should not a commanding grand general be exactly such a man!

sentences.zh: 姜維退駐鐘提。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei withdrew and encamped at Zhongti.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei withdrew and encamped at Zhongti.

sentences.zh: 初，吳大帝不立太廟，以武烈嘗為長沙太守，立廟於臨湘，使太守奉祠而已。

translations.literal: Previously, the Grand Emperor of Wu had not established an imperial ancestral temple; because Martial Splendor had once been governor of Changsha, a temple was set up at Linxiang, with the governor performing the sacrifices—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Grand Emperor of Wu had not established an imperial ancestral temple. Because Martial Splendor had once served as governor of Changsha, a shrine was built at Linxiang and the governor performed the rites—that was all.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，始作太廟於建業，尊大帝為太祖。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, an imperial ancestral temple was at last built at Jianye, and the Grand Emperor was honored as High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, an imperial ancestral temple was at last built at Jianye, and the Grand Emperor was honored as High Ancestor.
